semin-durr:105-105.t: His saying: {مِن بَعْدِ الذكر}: it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «كَتَبْنا», and it may be attached to «الزَّبُورِ» itself, because it has the sense of «المَزْبُور», i.e. "the written", i.e. "what was written after…". The mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «كَتَبْنا» is «أنَّ» together with what falls within its scope, i.e. "We wrote the inheritance of the earth by the righteous", i.e. We decreed it.

semin-durr:107-107.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ رَحْمَةً}: it may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for the sake of mercy". It may also be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), either by way of hyperbole, in that He made him mercy itself, or on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. «ذا رحمةٍ» ("possessing mercy"), or in the sense of «راحِم» ("merciful"). In the ḥadīth: «يا أيها الناسُ إنما أنا رحمةٌ مُهْداة» ("O people, I am only a mercy that has been gifted").
His saying: {لِّلْعَالَمِينَ}: it may be attached to an omitted element, as a ṣifa (adjective) of «رَحْمَةً», i.e. "being for the worlds". It may also be attached to «أَرْسَلْناك», according to those who hold it permissible for what comes after «إلاَّ» to be attached to what precedes it, or to an omitted element according to those who do not hold that. This is when the verb has not been left "emptied" (mufarragh) for what follows it; when it has been emptied, it is permissible, as in «ما مررتُ إلاَّ بزيدٍ» ("I passed by none but Zayd") — so said the Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] here. This is open to question, in that this too is emptied, because the "emptied" construction refers to the case where what follows «إلاَّ» needs what precedes it as its governor (ʿāmil).

semin-durr:108-108.t:
His saying: {أَنَّمَآ إلهكم}: «أنَّ» and what falls within its scope are in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) because they stand in place of the agent [of the passive verb, i.e. as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)], since the implied meaning is: "What is revealed to me is only the oneness of your God." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«إنَّما» is for restricting a judgement to a thing, or for restricting a thing to a judgement, as when you say «إنما زيدٌ قائم» ("Zayd is only standing") and «إنما يقومُ زيدٌ» ("Only Zayd stands"). Both examples are combined in this verse, because {إِنَّمَآ يوحى إِلَيَّ} together with its agent is on a par with «إنما يقومُ زيد», and {أَنَّمَآ إلهكم إله وَاحِدٌ} is on a par with «إنَّما زيد قائم». The benefit of combining them is to indicate that the revelation to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is restricted to Allah's having oneness exclusively to Himself."
The Shaykh said: "As for what he mentioned about «أنَّما» being for restriction as he described, this rests on «أنَّما» being for ḥaṣr (restriction). We have established that it is not for restriction, and that «ما» with «أنَّ» is like it with «كأنَّ» and with «لعلَّ»: just as it does not convey restriction in comparison, nor restriction in hoping, likewise it does not convey it with «أنَّ». As for his making «أنما» with the hamza vowelled with fatḥa like the one with kasra in indicating restriction, we know of no disagreement except regarding «إنما» with kasra. As for «أنما» with fatḥa, it is a maṣdar-forming particle from which, together with what follows it, a maṣdar (verbal noun) is formed, so the clause after it is not an independent clause. And if «أنما» indicated restriction, it would follow that one must say: nothing was revealed to him except tawḥīd, and restriction in that is not sound, since things other than tawḥīd were revealed to him."
I say: restriction in every context is according to what suits it. This context may require restriction in the revelation of oneness because of something that took place — the disbelievers' denial of His oneness, exalted is He — and [their claim] that Allah had revealed nothing to him about it. This is just as people have answered this difficulty that the Shaykh raised regarding the saying of the Exalted: {إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرٌ} [al-Raʿd: 7], {إِنَّمَآ أَنَاْ بَشَرٌ} [al-Kahf: 110], {إِنَّمَا الحياة الدنيا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ} [Muḥammad 36], and others. As for «ما» in His saying {إِنَّمَآ يوحى}, two views are possible. First: that it is the restraining (kāffa) «ما», as has preceded. Second: that it is a relative noun, as in His saying {إِنَّمَا صَنَعُواْ} [Ṭāhā: 69], and the khabar (predicate) is the clause {أَنَّمَآ إلهكم إله وَاحِدٌ}, the implied meaning being: "That which is revealed to me is this judgement."
His saying: {فَهَلْ أَنتُمْ مُّسْلِمُونَ}: a question whose meaning is a command, in the sense of «أَسْلِموا» ("submit!"), like His saying {فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُّنتَهُونَ} [al-Māʾida: 91], i.e. "Desist!"

semin-durr:109-109.t:
His saying: {آذَنتُكُمْ}: i.e. "I have informed you". The hamza in it is for transfer [to the causative]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«آذن» is transferred from «أَذِنَ» when it means "to know", but its use has become frequent in the sense of warning (indhār). From it is His saying, exalted is He: {فَأْذَنُواْ بِحَرْبٍ} [al-Baqara: 279], and the saying of Ibn Ḥilliza:
3367 - آذَنَتْنا بِبَيْنِها أسماءُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Asmāʾ informed us of her parting …)"
I say: the detailed treatment of this has preceded in al-Baqara.
His saying: {على سَوَآءٍ}: in the position of the accusative (naṣb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from both the agent and the object together, i.e. "being equal in knowledge of what I informed you of", not having concealed it from any one of them.
His saying: {وَإِنْ أدري}: the majority read with the yāʾ left quiescent, since there is nothing requiring otherwise. It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read «وإنْ أَدْريَ أقريبٌ» and «وَإِنْ أَدْرِيَ لَعَلَّهُ فِتْنَةٌ» with fatḥa on both yāʾs. This has been explained as likening it to the yāʾ of the first-person possessive. However, Ibn Mujāhid rejected this reading entirely. Ibn Jinnī said: "It is an error, because «إنْ» is negating and has no governing effect." Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted from someone else that he said in explaining it: "He cast the vowel of the hamza onto the yāʾ, so it became vowelled and the hamza remained quiescent; it was then changed into an alif because what precedes it has fatḥa, and then it was changed into a vowelled hamza, because it is in the status of something one begins with, and beginning with a quiescent letter is impossible." This is a strained explanation for which there is no need. Attributing error to the one who transmitted it from Ibn ʿAbbās is more fitting than this strain, for it is an anomalous (shādhdh), rejected reading. And this explanation, even if it helps with the first [instance], is of no use at all in the second. You will come across something close to the claim of changing the hamza into an alif and then changing the alif into a hamza in His saying {مِنسَأَتَهُ} [Sabaʾ: 14], if Allah the Exalted wills, and by that the matter of the explanation mentioned becomes easier.
The interrogative clause is in the position of the accusative by «أدْري», because it is suspended (muʿallaq) from governing [overtly]. The thing asked about was placed last because it is a verse-ending (fāṣila). Had it been placed in the middle, the construction would have been «أقريب ما تُوعدون أم بعيدٌ», but it was put last out of regard for the verse-endings.
As for {مَّا تُوعَدُونَ}, it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with what precedes it being a khabar (predicate) of it and a maʿṭūf (conjoined) element upon it. Abū al-Baqāʾ also allowed that it be nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of «قريبٌ». He said: "because it relies on the hamza [of interrogation]." He said: "And according to the view of the Basrans it may be explained as being nominative by «بعيد», because it is nearer to it." I say: he means that the question may be one of tanāzuʿ (two governors contending for one governed word), for each of the two adjectives can properly govern «ما تُوْعَدون» in terms of meaning.

semin-durr:110-110.t: His saying: {مِنَ القول}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الجهر».

semin-durr:111-111.t: His saying: {لَعَلَّهُ فِتْنَةٌ}: the apparent sense is that this clause suspends (taʿlīq) «أَدْري» [from governing overtly]. The Kufans treat hoping (tarajjī) like interrogation in that respect, except that the grammarians have not counted «لعلَّ» among the suspending elements, though it is evidently so, as in this verse and in His saying {وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يزكى} [ʿAbasa: 3] and {وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّ الساعة قَرِيبٌ} [al-Shūrā: 17].

semin-durr:112-112.t:
His saying: {قَالَ}: Ḥafṣ read «قال» as a report about the Messenger, upon him be peace. The rest read «قل» as a command. The majority read «رَبِّ» with kasra on the bāʾ, making do with the kasra in place of the first-person possessive yāʾ, and this is the most eloquent. Abū Jaʿfar read it with ḍamma on the bāʾ, and the author of al-Lawāmiḥ said: "It is a singular munādā (one addressed)." Then he said: "Omitting the vocative particle in what may be a description of «أَيّ» is far-fetched; its place is poetry." I say: this is not a case of the singular munādā; rather, some have stated explicitly that this is one of the permissible dialectal forms of a noun annexed to the first-person yāʾ when it is addressed in the vocative.
The majority read «احْكُمْ» in the form of a command. Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima and Ibn Yaʿmar read «رَبِّيْ» with the yāʾ quiescent and «أَحْكَمُ» as an elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl), so the two are mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).
It has also been read «أَحْكَمَ» with fatḥa on the mīm, like «ألزَمَ», as a past verb, also in the position of khabar for «ربِّي». The majority read «تَصِفُوْن» in the second person. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited to Ubayy, may Allah be pleased with him, «يَصِفُون» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, and this is also transmitted from ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir. The third person and the second person are both clear.

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {أَن تَمِيدَ} is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), meaning "that it not sway"; the «لا» was omitted because the meaning makes it understood, or (it means) "out of dislike that it sway". Abū al-Baqāʾ gave it the implied form "for fear that it sway" (مخافةَ أن تميدَ). There is room for objection in this, because if we make the fear attributed to the addressees, one of the conditions for the accusative of the mafʿūl lahu is impaired, namely (that it be) the agent; and if we make it attributed to the agent of the "making", that is impossible, because fear is not ascribed to Him, blessed and exalted is He. It may be said: it is preferred that the fear be attributed to the addressees. (Reply to) your statement "one of the conditions of the accusative is impaired": the answer is that it is not accusative at all, but genitive by the implied preposition of cause. And omitting the preposition is regular with «أنْ» and «أنَّ» when their condition is met.

His saying: {فِجَاجاً سُبُلاً}: there are two views on «فجاجاً». The first: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and «سُبُلا» is a badal (substitute) for it. The second: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «سبلاً», because originally it is an adjective of it; when it was put first it became accusative as a ḥāl, as in his saying:

3338 - لميَّةَ موحشاً طَلَلُ ... يلوحُ كأنَّه خِلَلُ
(For Mayya there is a ruin, desolate, gleaming as though it were sheath-linings.)

This is indicated by its occurring as an adjective in the other verse, namely the saying of the Exalted: {لِّتَسْلُكُواْ مِنْهَا سُبُلاً فِجَاجاً} [Nūḥ: 20]. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: «الفجاج» carries the sense of an adjective, so why was it put before «السُّبُل» and not placed after, as in the saying of the Exalted {لِّتَسْلُكُواْ مِنْهَا سُبُلاً فِجَاجاً}? I say: it was not put first as an adjective; rather it was made a ḥāl, as in his saying:

3339 - لِعَزَّةَ مُوْحِشاً طَلَلٌ قديمُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(For ʿAzza, desolate, an ancient ruin ... [the rest of the verse is elided in the source].)

If you say: what is the difference between the two in meaning? I say: one of them is an announcement that He made wide roads in it; the other is that when He created it He created it with that attribute, so it is an elucidation of what was left vague there."

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "By vagueness he means that the attribute does not necessarily have to be one with which the thing described is characterised at the time of reporting about it, although most often it is established in it at the time of reporting about it. Do you not see that one says: «I passed by Waḥshī, the killer of Ḥamza», and at the time of passing the killing of Ḥamza was not established in him?"

al-Fajj means the wide road; the plural is al-fijāj.

The pronoun in «فيها» may refer back to «الأرض» (the earth), which is the apparent (reading), as in His saying: {والله جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الأرض بِسَاطاً لِّتَسْلُكُواْ مِنْهَا سُبُلاً فِجَاجاً} [Nūḥ: 19-20]; and it may refer back to «الرواسي» (the firmly set mountains), meaning that He made wide roads in the mountains.

semin-durr:32-32.t: His saying: {وَهُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِهَا}: a resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya) clause; making it an implied (muqaddara) ḥāl is weak. Mujāhid and Ḥumayd read «عن آيتِها» in the singular form: he made creation a single sign, though it comprises many signs; or he used the singular and meant the genus.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {كُلٌّ}: that is, each of the two, namely the sun and the moon; or each of them, namely of the night, the day, the sun and the moon. «يَسْبَحون» may be the khabar of «كلٌ» according to the sense, and «في فلك» is attached to it; it may also be a ḥāl, with the khabar being the preposition phrase «في فَلك». What I have mentioned, that the muḍāf ilayhi may be implied as the four things mentioned, was stated by Abū al-Baqāʾ. Others did not mention anything except that the muḍāf ilayhi is the sun and the moon. That is the apparent view, because swimming/floating (sibāḥa) is an attribute of those two and not of the night and the day. On this basis an excuse must be offered for the use of the plural pronoun and for its being the plural of rational beings (man yaʿqil).

As for the first: it was said that it is plural only because there is an omitted conjoined item (maʿṭūf), its implied form being "and the stars", as other verses indicate. al-Zamakhsharī said: "The pronoun is for the sun and the moon, and what is meant by them is the genus of risings every day and night; they made them many because their points of rising are many, and that is the reason for pluralising them as 'suns' and 'moons'." End of quotation. What made that appealing is its being the end of a verse.

Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «يَسْبَحُون» is the khabar of «كلٌ» according to the sense, because when each one floats, all of them float. It was also said: on this view «يَسْبَحُون» is a ḥāl and the khabar is «في فَلَكٍ».

It was also said: the implied form is "kulluhā" (all of them) and the khabar is «يَسْبَحُون», the plural pronoun having come according to the sense of «كل». There is room for objection in this statement, in that when he allowed the muḍāf ilayhi to be two things, he made the khabar the preposition phrase and «يَسْبَحون» a ḥāl, to avoid the lack of agreement between khabar and mubtadaʾ; and so he fell into a disagreement between the ḥāl and its ṣāḥib.

As for the second (the question of rationality): because he ascribed to them swimming/floating, which is among the acts of rational beings, he pluralised them with the plural of rational beings, as in His saying: {رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَاجِدِينَ} [Yūsuf: 4] and {أَتَيْنَا طَآئِعِينَ} [Fuṣṣilat: 11].

This clause may have no grammatical position because it is resumptive. It may also be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. If we say that floating is ascribed to the night and the day, as was reported earlier from Abū al-Baqāʾ in one of the two views, then it is a ḥāl from all of them. If its attribution to them is not valid, it is a ḥāl from the sun and the moon. The interpretation of the plural has already been given. The Shaykh said: "Or its position is accusative as a ḥāl from the sun and the moon, because the night and the day are not characterised as running in an orbit; it is like your saying: «I saw Zayd and Hind adorned (mutabarrija)»." End. al-Zamakhsharī had already preceded him in this and he quoted it from him, meaning that evidence has shown that the ḥāl belongs to some of what came before, as in the example given.

al-Sibāḥa means swimming in water. It may be used to express going in general. Its derivation has already been given at «سُبْحانك».

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {أَفَإِيْن مِّتَّ}: a parallel has already been given in Āl ʿImrān at His saying: {أَفَإِيْن مَّاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ انقلبتم} [verse 144]. This verse contains evidence for the position of Sībawayh, which is that when a condition and a question are combined, the condition is answered. So in this verse the interrogative hamza has entered upon the conditional clause. The clause joined with the fāʾ is the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis), and it is not the point on which the question falls. Yūnus claimed that the question falls on the clause joined with the fāʾ, that the condition is parenthetical between the question and it, and that its apodosis is omitted. That is nothing, since had it been as he said, the construction would have been: «أفإن مِتَّ هم الخالدون» without a fāʾ. It seems Ibn ʿAṭiyya followed the line of Yūnus, for he said: "The interrogative alif enters, in meaning, upon the apodosis."

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {فِتْنَةً}: there are three views on its being accusative. The first: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl, that is, "fātinīn" (testing). The third: it is a maṣdar from the meaning of the governing verb, not from its form, because ibtilāʾ (trial) is fitna; so it is as if it had been said: "We try you (a trial)".

The majority read «تُرْجَعُوْن» with the tāʾ of address, in the passive. Others read it with the yāʾ of the third person, as a shift of person (iltifāt).

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {إِن يَتَّخِذُونَكَ}: «إنْ» here is negative, and it together with what is in its scope is the apodosis of the condition introduced by «إذا». «إذا» differs from the particles of condition in this respect: whenever the particles of condition are answered by a negative «إنْ» or a negative «ما», a fāʾ must be brought, so you say: «إن أَتَيْتَني فإنْ أَهَنْتُك» and «فما أَهَنْتُك»; but you say «إذا أَتَيْتَني ما أَهَنْتُك» without a fāʾ. This is indicated by His saying: {وَإِذَا تتلى عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ مَّا كَانَ حُجَّتَهُمْ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُواْ} [al-Jāthiya: 25].

«اتَّخَذَ» here is transitive to two objects. «هُزُوا» is the second: either by omission of a muḍāf, or by description with a maṣdar for emphasis, or by its taking the place of a passive participle.

There are two views on the apodosis of «إذا». The first: it is the negative «إنْ» (clause), as already stated. The second: it is omitted, and it is the saying with which the interrogative clause is reported in His saying {أهذا الذي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ}, since the implied form is: "and when those who disbelieved see you they say: «Is this the one who mentions your gods?»". On this view the negated clause is parenthetical between the protasis and its implied apodosis.

His saying: {وَهُمْ بِذِكْرِ الرحمن هُمْ كَافِرُونَ}: the first «هم» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «كافرون», and «بِذكْر» is attached to the khabar; the implied order is: "and they are disbelievers in the mention of...". The second «هم» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first, a verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī), so there occurs a separation between the governing element and what it governs by the emphasiser, and between the emphasised and the emphasiser by the governed element.

There are two views on this clause. The first: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of the implied saying, i.e. "they say that while they are in this state". The second: it is a ḥāl from the agent of «يَتَّخِذونك», which is the line al-Zamakhsharī took; he said: "The clause is in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. they take you as a mockery while they are in a state which is the root of mockery and ridicule, namely disbelief in Allah."

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {مِنْ عَجَلٍ}: there are two views on it. The first: it is a case of qalb (inversion). The original is: "haste (al-ʿajal) was created from man", because of how strongly it issues from him and how constantly it accompanies him. Abū ʿAmr took this view. It may be supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh «خُلِقَ العَجَلُ من الإِنسانِ», in which the inversion is present. The poet said:

3340 - حَسَرْتُ كَفِّيْ عن السِّربالِ آخُذُه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I bared my palm from the shirt, grasping it ... [the rest is elided in the source].)

He means: "I bared the shirt from my palm." Similar in speech: «إذا طَلَعَت الشِّعْرى استوى العُوْدُ على الحِرْباء» ("when Sirius rises, the stick levels on the chameleon"), and they said «عَرَضْتُ الناقةَ على الحَوْضِ» ("I presented the she-camel to the trough"). I have already given other examples of it. However, some restrict it to poetic necessity, and I have already given three positions on it.

The second: there is no inversion in it, and there are interpretations, the best of which is that this is for exaggeration: the very person of man is made as if created out of haste itself, to indicate how strongly man is characterised by it, and that it is his material from which he was taken. Similar in exaggeration, from the side of negation, is his saying, peace be upon him: «لستُ من الدَّدِ، ولا الدَّدُ مني» ("I am not of play, nor is play of me"). al-Dad means play. There are several forms of it: «دَدٌ» with the final lām omitted, «ددا» shortened like «عصا», and «دَدَن» with a nūn. Its alif, in one of its forms, is of unknown origin; we do not know whether it comes from a yāʾ or a wāw.

It was also said: al-ʿajal is clay, in the language of Ḥimyar. Abū ʿUbayda recited in support of that a verse by one of them:

3341 - النَّبْعُ في الصَّخْرةِ الصَّمَّاء مَنْبِتُه ... والنَّخْلُ مَنْبِتُه في الماءِ والعَجَلِ
(The nabʿ tree grows in the solid rock; the palm grows in water and clay [ʿajal].)

al-Zamakhsharī, after reciting the second half of this verse, said: "Allah knows best whether it is authentic", and he is excused.

This prepositional phrase may be attached to «خُلِقَ», in the figurative or the literal sense given above; or it may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, as if it were said: "man was created hasty (ʿajilan)". So said Abū al-Baqāʾ. The first is preferable.

The majority read «خُلِق» in the passive, with «الإِنسانُ» nominative, standing in for the agent. Mujāhid, Ḥumayd and Ibn Muqsim read «خَلَقَ» in the active, with «الإِنسانَ» accusative as direct object.

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying: {متى هذا}: «متى» is a fronted khabar, so it is in the position of nominative. Some of the people of Kufa claimed that it is in the position of accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), and that the governing element is an implied verb which governs the nominative of «هذا»; the implied form being "when will this promise come?" or "when will it arrive?" and the like. The first is the well-known view.

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying: {لَوْ يَعْلَمُ}: its apodosis is implied, because that is more forceful as a threat. al-Zamakhsharī gave the implied form: "they would not have been in that state of disbelief, mockery and impatience; but their ignorance of it is what made it light in their eyes." Ibn ʿAṭiyya gave the implied form: "they would not have been impatient." al-Ḥūfī gave: "they would have hastened." Others gave: "they would have known the truth of the resurrection."

«حينَ» is a mafʿūl bihi of «عَلِموا» and is not accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf); that is, "if they knew the time when the fire is not held back". al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is also possible that «يعلمُ» is left without being made transitive, meaning: had they had knowledge and not been ignorant they would not have been impatient. Then «حينَ» is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. when they do not hold back the fire from their faces they will know that they were in falsehood." On this view «حين» is accusative as an adverbial, because he made the object of knowing «أنَّهم كانوا».

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "The apparent view is that the object of «يعلم» is omitted, as what precedes it indicates it, i.e. if those who disbelieved knew the coming of the promised thing about which they asked and which they sought to elicit. And «حين» is accusative by the object, which is «مجيءَ» (the coming). It may also be a case of iʿmāl (competing governors) with an omitted muḍāf, giving effect to the second. The meaning: if they knew the touch of the fire when they do not hold it back from their faces."

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {بَغْتَةً}: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "taking by surprise". The pronoun in «تَأْتيهم» refers to the fire. It was also said: it refers to «الحين» (the time), because it has the sense of the Hour. It was also said: to the Hour in which He brings them to the punishment. It was also said: to the promise, because it has the sense of the fire they were promised; al-Zamakhsharī said this, and there is strain in it.

al-Aʿmash read «بل يَأْتيهم» with the yāʾ of the third person, «بَغَتة» with fatḥa on the ghayn, and «فيَبْهَتُهُمْ» also with yāʾ. As for the yāʾ, he made the pronoun refer to «الحين» or to the promise. Some said: "It refers to the fire, and its pronoun was made masculine only because it has the sense of punishment; then he observed the wording «النار» and made it feminine in His saying «رَدَّها»."

His saying: {بَلْ تَأْتِيهِم}: an iḍrāb of transition (turning from one topic to another). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «بل» is an istidrāk (rectification) preceded by an implied negation, whose implied form is: "The signs do not come according to their demand." There is room for objection in this, because the implied form would then become: "the signs do not come to them according to their demand, rather they come to them suddenly", so that the apparent sense would be that the signs come suddenly, and that is certainly not what is meant. And if he meant the implied form to be: "rather the Hour or the fire comes to them", that does not conform to the rule of iḍrāb.

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His saying: {مِنَ الرحمن}: attached to «يَكْلؤُكم» with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "from the command of the Merciful" or "His might", as in: {يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِ الله} [al-Raʿd: 11]. «بالليل» means "in the night". al-Kilāʾa means protection. One says: «كَلأَه يَكْلَؤُه اللهُ كِلاءة» (Allah guarded him), with kasra on the kāf; al-Jawharī fixed it so. So he is kāliʾ (guard) and makluʾ (guarded). Ibn Harma said:

3342 - إنَّ سُلَيْمَى واللهُ يَكْلَؤُها ... ضَنَّتْ بشَيْءٍ ما كان يَرْزَؤها
(Indeed Sulaymā — and Allah guards her — was niggardly with something that would not have diminished her.)

«اكْتَلأْتُ منه» means "I guarded myself against him". From it vegetation is called kalaʾ, because by it the bodies of livestock are sustained and kept safe. One says: «بَلَّغَ الله بك أَكْلأَ العُمُرِ» (may Allah bring you to the safest [most protected] part of life). al-Mukallaʾ is a place where ships are kept safe. In the ḥadīth: "He forbade the sale of al-kāliʾ for al-kāliʾ", that is, the sale of debt for debt, as if each of the holders of the two debts watches (yaklaʾu) the other, that is, keeps an eye on him.

His saying: {بَلْ هُمْ}: an iḍrāb away from the negation contained in the first sentence, since the implied form is: "They have no guardian and no protector other than the Merciful."

al-Zuhrī and Ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read «يَكْلَوُكم» with a light ḍamma and without hamza. al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ reported «يَكْلَوْكم» with fatḥa on the lām and sukūn on the wāw; I did not know it as a reading. It is close to the dialect of those who lighten the hamza in «أكلَتْ الكلا على الكلَوْ» when pausing, except that he treated continuation like pause.

semin-durr:43-43.t: His saying: {أَمْ لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ}: «أم» is munqaṭiʿa (disconnected), i.e. "rather, do they have gods?" What concerns it has already been given. His saying: {مِّن دُونِنَا} has two views. The first: it is attached to «تَمْنَعُهم»; it was said that the meaning is: "Do they have gods who place them in protection and might?" al-Ḥūfī took this view. The second: it is attached to an omitted element because it is an adjective of «آلهة», i.e. "gods other than Us who protect them"; for that reason Ibn ʿAbbās said: "There is a fronting and a delaying in the sentence." His saying: {لاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ} is resumptive and has no position; it may also be an adjective of «آلهة», though that is remote in meaning.

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ يَسْمَعُ}: Ibn ʿĀmir read here «ولا تُسْمِعُ» with ḍamma on the tāʾ (second person address) and kasra on the mīm, with «الصُّمَّ» and «الدعاءَ» both accusative. Ibn Kathīr read likewise in al-Naml and al-Rūm. The rest of the Seven read it with fatḥa on the third-person yāʾ and on the mīm, «الصُّمُّ» nominative and «الدعاءَ» accusative, throughout the Qur'an.

al-Ḥasan read like the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir except with the third-person yāʾ; and Ibn Khālawayh transmitted from him «ولا يُسْمَعُ» with third-person yāʾ in the passive, «الصُّمُّ» nominative, «الدعاءَ» accusative. It is also transmitted from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ «ولا يُسْمِعُ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the mīm, «الصُّمَّ» accusative and «الدعاءُ» nominative.

As for the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir and Ibn Kathīr, the agent in it is the pronoun of the addressee, who is the Messenger, peace be upon him; «الصُّمَّ» and «الدعاءَ» are accusative as the two objects, the first of which is the agent in meaning. As for the reading of the majority, the verb is attributed to «الصُّمَّ», so «الدعاء» is accusative as direct object. As for the first reading of al-Ḥasan, the verb is attributed to the pronoun of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; it is like the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir in meaning. As for his second reading, the verb is attributed to «الصُّمُّ» standing in for the agent, so the second, «الدعاء», is accusative.

As for the reading of Abū ʿAmr, the verb is attributed to «الدعاء» by way of extension (ittisāʿ), and the second object is omitted because it is known; the implied form is: "the call does not make the deaf hear anything at all." When Abū al-Baqāʾ came to this passage he said: "«ولا يَسْمَعُ» has readings whose aspects are obvious", and he did not mention them.

And [as for his saying] «إذا»: there are two views on what makes it accusative. The first: it is «يَسْمَعُ». The second: it is «الدعاءُ», so he gave effect to the maṣdar defined with al-; and if they give it effect on a plain direct object, then on an adverbial it is more fitting.

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying: {نَفْحَةٌ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "In this there are three intensifications: the word «المَسّ» (touch), and what is in al-nafḥ of the sense of fewness and slightness. One says: «نَفَحَتْه الدابَّةُ» (the beast kicked him) when it kicked him a slight kick; and «نَفَحه بعَطيَّةٍ» means with a little gift; and the form of the single instance (bināʾ al-marra) of it, that is, at the least touch they submit. al-Nafḥ is a passing thought (khaṭra). «نَفَحَ له من عطائِه» means he gave him a small portion. The poet said:

3343 - إذا رَيْدَةٌ من حيث ما نَفَحَتْ له ... أتاه برَيَّاها خليلٌ يواصِلُهْ
(When a breeze from wherever it was blew toward him, a friend who keeps ties came to him with its fragrance.) [Translator's note: this gloss is tentative; the verse is difficult.]

{مِّنْ عَذَابِ} is an adjective of «نَفْحَة».

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying: {القسط}: there are two views on the accusative of «القِسْطَ». The first: it is an adjective of «الموازين»; on this view, why is it singular? There are two answers. One: it is originally a maṣdar, and a maṣdar is singular in every case. The other: it is with an omitted muḍāf. The second view: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. "for the sake of justice". There is room for objection in this, however, in that when the mafʿūl lahu is defined with al-, it is rare for it to be bare of the preposition of cause. You say «جئتُ للإِكرام» ("I came for honouring"), and rarely «جئت الإِكرامَ», as in the saying of another:

3344 - لا أَقْعُدُ الجبنَ عن الهَيْجاءِ ... ولو توالَتْ زُمَرُ الأعداءِ
(I do not hold back from battle out of cowardice, even if the troops of the enemy follow one another.)

«القِصْطَ» with ṣād was also read, because of the ṭāʾ; this has already been given.

His saying: {لِيَوْمِ القيامة}: there are several aspects of this lām. The first: al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is like it in your saying «جِئْتُ لخمسٍ خَلَوْنَ من الشهر» (I came on the fifth day since the month began), and from it is the verse of al-Nābigha:

3345 - تَوَهَّمْتُ آياتٍ لها فَعَرَفْتُها ... لستةِ أعوام وذا العامُ سابعُ
(I made out signs of hers and recognised them after six years, and this year is the seventh.)"

The second: it has the sense of «في» ("in"). Ibn Qutayba and Ibn Mālik took this view, and it is the opinion of the Kufans. In their view, from it is: {لاَ يُجَلِّيهَا لِوَقْتِهَآ إِلاَّ هُوَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 187], and the saying of Miskīn al-Dārimī:

3346 - أولئك قومي قد مضَوْا لسبيلِهم ... كما قد مضى مِنْ قبلُ عادٌ وتُبَّعُ
(Those are my people; they have gone their way, as ʿĀd and Tubbaʿ went before.)

and the saying of another:

3347 - وكلُّ أبٍ وابنٍ وإنْ عُمِّرا معاً ... مُقِيْمَيْنِ مفقودٌ لوقتٍ وفاقدُ
(Every father and son, even if they live long together, abiding, one is lost at a set time and one is bereaved.)

The third: it is on its usual footing as a lām of cause, but with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "for the reckoning of the Day of Resurrection."

His saying: {شَيْئاً}: it may be a second object, and it may be a maṣdar, i.e. "anything of wrong".

His saying: {مِثْقَال}: Nāfiʿ read here and in Luqmān «مِثْقال» in the nominative, on the basis that «كان» is complete (tāmma), i.e. "even if a weight is found". The others read it in the accusative, on the basis that it is incomplete (nāqiṣa), its subject being latent, i.e. "even if [the deed] were". {مِّن خَرْدَلٍ} is an adjective of «حَبَّة».

The majority read «أَتَيْنَا» from al-itiyān with a short hamza, i.e. "We brought it". Ibn Masʿūd read likewise, and that is an explanation of the meaning, not a recitation. Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Saʿīd, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Sayyāba and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad read «آتَيْنا» with a long hamza. There are several aspects to it. First, and it is the sound one: it is fāʿalnā from al-muʾātāt, which is recompense and requital; the meaning: "We recompensed with it", and for that reason it is made transitive with the bāʾ. Second: it is mufāʿala from al-itiyān, in the sense of recompense and requital, because they came to Him with deeds and He came to them with the recompense; al-Zamakhsharī said this. Third: it is afʿala from al-ītāʾ (giving); so some imagined, and it is a mistake. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "If «آتَيْنا» meant «أعطينا» (We gave), it would not be made transitive by a preposition. What weakens this reading is that replacing a fatḥa-vowelled wāw with a hamza is not known; it is known only for the ḍamma-vowelled and the kasra-vowelled." He means that this reader should have read «واتَيْنا» like «واظَبْنا», since it is from al-muwātāt on the sound view; so this reader replaced the fatḥa-vowelled wāw with a hamza. That is rare, and from it «واتاه» was taken.

Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is read with the long hamza meaning 'We recompensed with it'; it is close to the meaning of «أَعْطَيْنا» (We gave), because recompense is giving, and it is not derived from «أَتَيْنا», because that was not reported from them."

Ḥumayd read «أَثَبْنا» from al-thawāb (reward). The pronoun in «بها» refers to «المِثْقال», and its pronoun is feminine because of its being annexed to a feminine, like the saying:

3348 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كما شَرِقَتْ صدرُ القناةِ من الدَّمِ
(... as the chest of the lance was choked with blood.) [Translator's note: the first half of the verse is elided in the source. The closing words of the entry, «في اكتسابِه بالإِضافةِ التأنيثَ», are a fragment of the author's remark, "in its acquiring the feminine through annexation".]

semin-durr:48-48.t: His saying: {وَضِيَآءً وَذِكْراً}: it may be a case of ʿaṭf al-ṣifāt (conjoining of attributes), so that one thing is meant by it, i.e. "We gave him the one that combines these things". It was also said: the wāw is redundant (zāʾida). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "On this view «ضياءً» is a ḥāl."

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {الذين يَخْشَوْنَ}: for its position there are three aspects, namely genitive as an adjective, or a badal, or an explicative apposition (bayān); and nominative or accusative by qaṭʿ (cutting off).

semin-durr:51-51.t:
His saying: {رُشْدَهُ}: a second object. The majority read «رُشْدَه» with ḍamma on the rā' and sukūn on the shīn. ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read both with fatḥa. Discussion of both has already been given.

His saying: {مِن قَبْلُ}: that is, before Mūsā and Hārūn. This is the best implied form for the muḍāf ilayhi. It was also said: before his maturity or his prophethood. The pronoun in «به» refers to Ibrāhīm. It was also said: to «رُشْدَه».

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying: {إِذْ قَالَ}: it may be accusative by «آتَيْنا», or by «رُشْدَه», or by «عالمين», or by an implied verb, i.e. "remember the time of his saying". Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that it be a badal from the place of «قبلُ», meaning that it takes its place so that the meaning is sound, since the implied form becomes: "We gave him his right guidance when he said". On this implied form it is remote in meaning.

His saying: {لَهَا}: it was said that the lām is causal, i.e. "devoted for their sake". It was also said: it has the sense of «على», i.e. "devoted to them". It was also said: «عاكفون» was made to include the meaning of "worshippers", which is why the lām was brought. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: it was also said that it conveys the sense of specification. al-Zamakhsharī said: "He did not intend any omitted object for «العاكفين»", and he treated it as an intransitive, as in "doers of devotion (fāʿilūn al-ʿukūf)". I say: it is preferable that the lām be causal and the complement of «عاكفون» be omitted, i.e. "devoted to them for their sake and not for anything else".

al-Tamāthīl is the plural of timthāl, which is a figure made of marble, copper or wood, made in resemblance to the creation of man or other animals. Imruʾ al-Qays said:

3349 - فيا رُبَّ يومٍ قد لَهَوْتُ وليلةٍ ... بآنِسَةٍ كأنَّها خَطُّ تمثالِ
(How many a day and night I have sported with a gentle, friendly girl, as if she were the outline of a statue.)

semin-durr:53-53.t: His saying: {لَهَا عَابِدِينَ}: «عابدين» is the second object of «وَجَدْنا», and «لها» has nothing it is attached to, because the lām is redundant on the direct object on account of its being fronted.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying: {أَنتُمْ}: a tawkīd (emphasis) of the attached pronoun. al-Zamakhsharī said: "«وأنتم» is among the emphases without which the speech is not sound, because conjoining to a pronoun that is in the status of part of the verb is not permitted. Similar is {اسكن أَنْتَ وَزَوْجُكَ الجنة} [al-Baqara: 35]." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This is not a rule agreed upon, so that the speech would not be sound without it; for the Kufans allow conjoining to the attached nominative pronoun without emphasis by the detached pronoun and without a separator. His comparing it with {اسكن أَنْتَ وَزَوْجُكَ الجنة} is contrary to his own school's position on {اسكن أَنْتَ وَزَوْجُكَ}, since his school claims that «وزوجُك» is not conjoined to the latent pronoun in «اسكُنْ», but is nominative by an implied verb, i.e. 'and let her dwell', so for him it is of the kind of conjoining of clauses; and this statement of his is contrary to the position of Sībawayh."

I say: it does not follow that he went against his own school, since it is permissible to cite a parallel according to someone who holds that view, even if he himself does not hold it.

{فِي ضَلاَلٍ} may be the khabar if «كان» is incomplete, or attached to «كنتم» if it is complete.

semin-durr:55-55.t:
His saying: {بالحق}: attached to «جِئْتَ». The literal coming is not what is meant, since he was not absent. As for «أم أنت»: «أم» is muttaṣila (connected), even though a clause follows it, because the clause is in the status of a single word, since the implied form is: "Which of the two matters has occurred: your coming with the truth, or your playing?" As in the saying:

3350 - ما أبالي أنَبَّ بالحَزْنِ تَيْسٌ ... أم جفاني بظهرِ غَيْبٍ لئيمُ
(I do not care whether a buck bleated in the rough ground, or a base man slighted me behind my back.)

and the saying:

3351 - لَعَمْرُك ما أَدْرِي وإن كنتُ دارياً ... شُعَيْثُ بنُ سَهْمٍ أم شُعَيْثُ بنُ مِنْقَرِ
(By your life, I do not know, though I may be one who knows, whether it is Shuʿayth ibn Sahm or Shuʿayth ibn Minqar.)

He means: which of the two matters has occurred? Had it been munqaṭiʿa (disconnected), it would be construed as «بل» plus the hamza, and that is not what is meant.

semin-durr:56-56.t:
His saying: {الذي فطَرَهُنَّ}: it may be nominative in position, or accusative by qaṭʿ (cutting off). The accusative pronoun in «فَطَرَهُنَّ» refers to the heavens and the earth. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Since the heavens and the earth do not reach a large number, the pronoun came as the pronoun of the small number (qilla)." I say: if he means that each one of the heavens and the earth does not reach (a large number), that is granted, but it is not what is meant; rather the totality is meant. And if he means that the totality of the two does not reach it, that is not granted, because it reaches fourteen, which is within the range of the plural of large number (jamʿ al-kathra); unless we say that the earth is one single entity and not seven like the heaven, as some have held; then that would be sound for him, but it is not relied upon.

It was also said: it refers to the statues. al-Zamakhsharī said: "That it refers to the statues is firmer for showing them to be in error, and more thorough in arguing against them." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«فَطَرَهُنَّ» is an expression about them as though they were rational, and this is because of their obedience and submission, and they have been described in several places with the description of those who have reason." Another said: "«فَطَرَهُنَّ»: he returned the pronoun of rational beings because of the states issuing from them which indicate that they are of the kind of rational beings; for Allah the Exalted informed (us) by His saying {أَتَيْنَا طَآئِعِينَ} [Fuṣṣilat: 11], and by the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: «The heaven groaned, and it had a right to groan»."

I say: it is as though Ibn ʿAṭiyya and this speaker imagined that «هُنَّ» is among the pronouns specific to rational females, and that is not so; it is a word shared between the rational and others. The Exalted said: {مِنْهَآ أَرْبَعَةٌ حُرُمٌ} [al-Tawba: 36] and then said: {فَلاَ تَظْلِمُواْ فِيهِنَّ}.

His saying: {على ذلكم}: attached to an omitted element, or to «الشاهدين» by extension, or for clarification (ʿalā al-bayān). A parallel has already been given, such as: {لَكُمَا لَمِنَ الناصحين} [al-Aʿrāf: 21].

semin-durr:57-57.t:
His saying: {وتالله}: the majority read with the tāʾ of two dots above. Muʿādh ibn Jabal and Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal read it with the single-dotted bāʾ. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the difference between the bāʾ and the tāʾ? I say: the bāʾ is the original, and the tāʾ is a replacement for the wāw, which itself is a replacement for it; and the tāʾ has an added sense, namely wonder, as though he wondered at how easy the plot became at his hand and how it was made possible." As for his saying "the bāʾ is the original", this is indicated by its usage across the chapter, unlike the wāw and the tāʾ, even though al-Suhaylī rejected that the wāw is a replacement for it.

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Reasoning requires that each of them be an original. As for his saying «wonder», the texts of the grammarians say that wonder is permissible in it and not necessary, and it is necessary only with the lām, as in the saying:

3352 - للهِ يَبْقى على الأيَّامِ ذو حِيَدٍ ... بمُشْمَخِرّ به الظَّيَّانُ والآوسُ
(By Allah! — does a long-horned ibex endure through the days on a towering height where myrtle and ās-trees grow?) [lām of wonder]"

«بعدَ» is accusative by «لأَكِيْدَنَّ». «مُدْبرين» is a confirming ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), because «تُوَلُّوا» already conveys its meaning. The majority read «تُوَلُّوا» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and the lām, the imperfect of «ولّى» with shadda. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «تَوَلَّوا» with fatḥa on both, the imperfect of «تولّى»; the original is «تَتَوَلَّوا», and one of the two tāʾs was omitted: either the first, in the view of Hishām, or the second, in the view of the Basrans. It is supported by the reading of all in {فَتَوَلَّوْاْ عَنْهُ مُدْبِرِينَ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 90], and no one read «فَوَلَّوْا», which would be the analogue of the people's reading here. In both readings the lām of the word is omitted, namely the yāʾ, since it is from «وَلي».

What this verb is attached to is omitted, its implied form being: "you turn away to your festival", and the like.

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying: {جُذَاذاً}: the majority read «جُذاذاً» with ḍamma on the jīm. al-Kisāʾī read it with kasra, and Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Nahīk and Abū al-Sammāl with fatḥa. Quṭrub said: in all its dialects it is a maṣdar, so it is not dualised, pluralised or feminised. The apparent view is that the ḍamma form is a noun for the broken thing, like al-ḥuṭām, al-rufāt and al-futāt, meaning the thing that is shattered and crumbled. al-Yazīdī said: "The ḍamma form is the plural of juzādha with ḍamma, like zujāj in zujāja, and the kasra form is the plural of jadhīdh, like kirām in karīm." Some said: the fatḥa form is a maṣdar in the sense of the passive participle, i.e. "cut to pieces"; on this view it may be with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "possessors of fragments". It was also said: the ḍamma form is the plural of juzādha with ḍamma, the kasra form is the plural of jizādha with kasra, and the fatḥa form is a maṣdar.

Ibn Wathāb read «جُذُذاً» with two ḍammas and no alif between the two dhāls; it is the plural of jadhīdh, like qalīb and qulub. It was also read with ḍamma on the jīm and fatḥa on the dhāl. There are two aspects to it. The first: its original is two ḍammas, and it was lightened by replacing the ḍamma with fatḥa, like surar and dhulal as plurals of sarīr and dhalīl, and it is a dialect of Banū Kalb. The second: it is the plural of juddha, like futat for futta and durar for durra.

al-Jadhdh is cutting and breaking, and to it belongs the saying:

3353 - بنو المهلبِ جَذَّ اللهُ دابِرَهُمْ ... أَمْسَوْا رَماداً فلا أَصْلٌ ولا طَرَفُ
(The Banū al-Muhallab — may Allah cut off their last remnant — became ashes, with neither root nor branch.)

This was already covered in full in Hūd.

He brought «هم», the pronoun of rational beings, treating the idols as rational beings, since they held that belief about them.

His saying: {إِلاَّ كَبِيراً}: an exception from the accusative in «فَجَعَلهم», i.e. he did not break it but left it. «لهم» is an adjective of it, and the pronoun may refer to the idols; the explanation of the return of the pronoun of rational beings to them has been given. It may also refer to their worshippers. The pronoun in «إليه» may refer to Ibrāhīm, i.e. they will return to his statement when the truth becomes clear to them; and it may refer to the big one. Each has been said.

semin-durr:59-59.t: His saying: {مَن فَعَلَ}: «مَنْ» may be interrogative, and that is the apparent view. On this view the clause from His saying «إنَّه لمِن الظالمين» is resumptive and has no grammatical position. It may also be a relative noun meaning "the one who"; on this view the clause «إنَّه» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the relative. The implied form is: "The one who did this to our gods — indeed he...".

semin-durr:60-60.t:
His saying: {يَذْكُرُهُمْ}: concerning this clause [there are several aspects]. The first: «سمع» here takes two objects because it relates to a person (ʿayn), so «فتىً» is the first object and the clause «يَذْكُرُهم» is in the position of accusative as the second object. Do you not see that if you said «سمعتُ زيداً» and were silent, it would not be a speech, unlike «سمعت قراءتَه وحديثَه»? The second: it is also in the position of accusative, as an adjective of Ibrāhīm. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the status of the two verbs after «سمعنا», and what is the difference between them? I say: both are adjectives of «فَتىً»; except that the first, «يَذْكُرهم», is indispensable for «سَمِعَ», because you do not say «سمعت زيداً» and stop, until you mention something of what is heard; as for the second, it is not so."

I say: what he said is not necessarily so; for you know that «سَمِعَ», if it relates to what is heard, as in «سمعت مقالةَ بكرٍ», then there is no disagreement that it takes one object; and if it relates to what is not heard, it is again not sufficient by itself, without disagreement; rather something that is heard must be mentioned. So if you said «سمعتُ زيداً» and were silent, or «سمعتُ زيداً يركبُ», it would not be permissible. If you said «سمعتُه يَقْرأ» it is sound. There was disagreement among the grammarians on this: Abū ʿAlī makes it take two objects, and al-Zamakhsharī's statement does not hold up on his view; others make it take one object, and make the clause after a definite noun a ḥāl and after an indefinite one an adjective, and this is what al-Zamakhsharī meant.

His saying: {إِبْرَاهِيمُ}: there are several aspects to the nominative of «إبراهيمُ». The first: it is nominative as a deputy agent, i.e. "this word was said to him"; for that reason Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "What is meant is the name, not the named." There is disagreement among the grammarians on this question, I mean the governing of «قول» over a single word that neither conveys the meaning of a sentence, nor is cut from a sentence, nor is a maṣdar of «قال», nor an adjective of its maṣdar, as in «قلتُ زيداً», i.e. "I said this word". A group preferred it, such as al-Zajjājī, al-Zamakhsharī, Ibn Kharūf and Ibn Mālik, and others prohibited it. Among those who preferred the nominative of «إبراهيمُ» in the way I have mentioned are al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya. As for when the single word conveys the meaning of a sentence, as in their saying «قلتُ خطبةً وشعراً وقصيدةً», or is cut from a sentence, as in the saying:

3354 - إذا ذُقْتُ فاها قلت طعمُ مُدامَةٍ ... مُعَتَّقَةٍ ممَّا يجيءُ به التُّجُرْ
(When I tasted her mouth I said: the taste of an aged wine, of what the merchants bring.)

or is a maṣdar, as in «قلتُ قولاً», or an adjective of it, as in «قلتُ حقاً أو باطلاً», then «قول» governs it. So they said. In their statement "the single word cut from the sentence" there is room for objection, because the saying does not govern this; it governs only the sentence that contains it.

The second: it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is said to him: this is Ibrāhīm" or "he is Ibrāhīm". The third: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "it is said to him: Ibrāhīm is the one who did that". The fourth: it is vocative with the vocative particle omitted, i.e. "O Ibrāhīm"; on the three aspects (the second, third and fourth) it is cut from a sentence, and that sentence is quoted by «يُقال». The treatment of this has already been given in al-Baqara at {وَقُولُواْ حِطَّةٌ} [verse 58], nominative and accusative, and in al-Aʿrāf at His saying {قَالُواْ مَعْذِرَةً} [verse 164], nominative and accusative.

The clause «يُقال له» may be another object, as in your saying «ظننتُ زيداً كاتباً شاعراً»; and it may be an adjective, in the view of al-Zamakhsharī and those who followed him; and it may be a ḥāl from «فتى». That is permitted because it has been specified by the description.

semin-durr:61-61.t: His saying: {على أَعْيُنِ}: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «به», i.e. "bring him openly, uncovered, in their sight and view". al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the meaning of elevation in «على»? I say: it is used by way of metaphor, i.e. his coming is fixed in the eyes and settles there as a rider is settled on the mount and in command of it."

semin-durr:62-62.t: His saying: {أَأَنْتَ فَعَلْتَ}: there are two views on «أنت». The first: it is the agent of an implied verb that the overt verb after it explains; the implied form is: "Did you do this to our gods?" When the verb was omitted the pronoun became detached. The second: it is a mubtadaʾ, and the sentence after it is the khabar. The difference between the two views in wording is clear: the clause «فَعَلْتَ» that is pronounced has, on the first, no position because it is explanatory, and its position is nominative on the second. In meaning: when the interrogative enters upon the verb, it signals that the doubt is attached to it: did it happen or not, without doubt about its agent; and when it enters upon the noun, the doubt falls on it: is it the agent or someone else, while the occurrence of the verb is not in doubt, but is simply taken as having occurred. So if you say «أقام زيدٌ؟» your doubt is about his standing; and if you say «أزيدٌ قام؟» and make it a mubtadaʾ, your doubt is whether the act issued from him or from ʿAmr. The first view is the preferred one among the grammarians, because what the verb requires, namely the interrogative particle, precedes it.

semin-durr:63-63.t:
His saying: {بَلْ فَعَلَهُ}: this iḍrāb is away from an omitted clause whose implied form is: "I did not do it; the agent in truth is Allah the Exalted, rather he did it." Attributing the act to "their big one" is among the most forceful of indirect expressions (maʿārīḍ).

His saying: {هذا}: there are six aspects to it. The first: it is an adjective of «كبيرُهم». The second: it is a badal from «كبيرُهم». The third: it is the khabar of «كبيرهم», on the basis that the speech is complete at His saying {بَلْ فَعَلَهُ}, and the agent of the verb is omitted. So Abū al-Baqāʾ reported, and said: "This is remote, because omitting the agent is not permissible." I say: this view is ascribed to al-Kisāʾī, and in that case it is not good to answer him by pointing to the omission of the agent, for he permits it and holds to it, and makes the implied form: "rather whoever did it did it". It may be that he meant by "omission" the implicit pronoun (iḍmār), since when the agent was not mentioned in the wording it was called an omission.

The fourth: the agent is the pronoun for «فتى». The fifth: the agent is the pronoun for «إبراهيمُ». These two aspects support what I mentioned, that the one who said "omission of the agent" may have meant only the implicit pronoun. The sixth: «فَعَلَه» is not a verb; rather the fāʾ is a conjunction that entered upon «عَلَّ», whose original is «لعلَّ», a particle of hope. The omission of the first lām is established, so the wording became «فَعَلَّه», i.e. «فَلَعَلَّه»; then the first lām was omitted and the second lightened. This is ascribed to al-Farrāʾ. It is a view turned away from. He argued for his school by the reading of Ibn al-Samayfaʿ «فَعَلَّه» with shadda on the lām, which is anomalous (shādhdha), and the well-known reading is not referred back to it. It seems that what led them to this was the obscurity of the grounds for this speech coming from the Prophet, peace be upon him.

His saying: {إِن كَانُواْ يِنْطِقُونَ}: its apodosis is omitted, as what precedes it indicates it. Whoever permits fronting makes «فسألوهم» the apodosis.

semin-durr:65-65.t:
His saying: {ثُمَّ نُكِسُواْ على رُءُوسِهِمْ}: the majority read «نُكِسُوا» in the passive with the kāf light, i.e. "Allah turned them upside down" or "made them ashamed". {على رُءُوسِهِمْ} is a ḥāl, i.e. "being upon their heads". It may also be attached to the verb itself.

al-Naks and al-tanqīs mean inversion. One says «نَكَس رأسَه» and «نَكَّسه», light or with shadda, i.e. he bowed it down until its top became its bottom. Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, Ibn al-Jārūd and Ibn Muqsim read «نُكِّسوا» with shadda. It has already been given that this is a dialect form of the light one, so the shadda is neither for transitivity nor for intensity. Riḍwān ibn ʿAbd al-Maʿbūd read «نَكَسُوا» light, in the active; on this the object is omitted, its implied form being: "they bowed their own selves upon their heads".

Their saying: {لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ}: this clause is the answer to an omitted oath, and the oath and its answer are both governed by an implied saying; that implied saying is a ḥāl from the nominative of «نُكِسُوا», i.e. "they were turned upside down, saying: By Allah, you certainly knew".

His saying: {مَا هؤلاء يَنطِقُونَ}: this «ما» may be Hijāzī, in which case «هؤلاء» is its subject and «يَنْطِقون» is in the position of accusative as its predicate; or Tamīmī, in which case it has no effect. The whole negated clause stands in for the two objects if «عَلِمْتَ» is used in its usual sense, and for one object if it is of the sense of "recognising" (ʿirfāniyya).

semin-durr:67-67.t: The discussion of «أف» and its dialects has already been given in Subḥān (al-Isrāʾ). The lām in «لكم» and in «لِما» is the lām of clarification (tabyīn), i.e. "the saying of uff is for you, not for others", and it is the parallel of {هَيْتَ لَكَ} [Yūsuf: 23].

semin-durr:69-69.t:
His saying: {بَرْداً}: that is, "possessing coolness". The apparent view of «سلاماً» is that it is conjoined to «بَرْدا», so it is a khabar of «كوني». Some allowed that it be accusative as a maṣdar, intended as the customary greeting. This was rejected on the ground that had that been intended, the nominative would have been preferable, as in the saying of Ibrāhīm: {سَلاَمٌ} [Hūd: 69]. That is not binding, for the Qur'an may come in the eloquent and the more eloquent form. This is indicated by its having come in the accusative when the greeting was intended, as in the saying of the angels: {قَالُواْ سَلاَماً} [Hūd: 69].

His saying: {على إِبْرَاهِيمَ} is attached to «سلام» itself if the greeting is intended. It may also be an adjective, and so be attached to an omitted element. On this it is possible that he omitted the adjective of the first because the adjective of the second indicates it, the implied form being: "be coolness upon him and safety upon him".

semin-durr:71-71.t: His saying: {وَلُوطاً}: two views are allowed. The first: it is conjoined to the object before it. The second: it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). The first is preferable. His saying: {إِلَى الأرض}: two views are allowed. The first: it is attached to «نَجَّيْناه», on the basis that it includes the meaning "We brought him out by deliverance"; since it included the meaning of "brought out", it was made transitive as that is. The second: there is no inclusion of meaning in it, and the preposition is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «نَجَّيْناه», i.e. "We delivered him, arriving at the land". So the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] gave the implied form. There is room for objection in it, in that he implied a restricted "being" (kawn muqayyad), and he often objects to al-Zamakhsharī and others for that.

semin-durr:72-72.t:
His saying: {نَافِلَةً}: in the explanation of al-nāfila it was said: it is a gift. It was also said: an increase. It was also said: a grandchild. On the first, it is accusative in the manner of maṣdars, from the meaning of the governing verb, «وهبنا», and not from its form, since "bestowing" (hiba) and "giving" are close; it is like al-ʿāqiba and al-ʿāfiya. On the last two, it is accusative as a ḥāl, and what is meant by it is Yaʿqūb. al-Nāfila is specific to Yaʿqūb on every reading, because Isḥāq was his (Ibrāhīm's) own son from his loins.

His saying: {وَكُلاًّ}: the first object of «جَعَلْنا», and «صالحين» is the second; the governing verb is in the middle between them. The original is: "We made, that is, We turned each of Ibrāhīm and those mentioned with him into righteous ones."

semin-durr:73-73.t:
His saying: {وَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ أَئِمَّةً}: as given earlier, except that the governing verb was not placed in the middle. «يَهْدون» is an adjective of «أئمة». «بأَمْرِنا» is attached to «يَهْدُون». The morphology concerning the word «أئمة» and the readers' readings of it have already been given.

His saying: {فِعْلَ الخيرات}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its original is «أن تُفْعَلَ الخيراتُ» ('that good deeds be done'), then «فِعْلاً الخيراتِ», then «فِعْلَ الخيراتِ», and likewise «وإقامَ الصلاة وإيتاءَ الزكاةِ»." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "It seems that when al-Zamakhsharī saw that doing good deeds, establishing prayer and giving zakāh are not rulings specific to those to whom revelation was sent, but that they and others share in this, he made the verb passive, so that the maṣdar would not, in meaning, be annexed to the pronoun of those to whom revelation was sent, which would make the implied form: 'their doing good deeds, their establishing prayer, their giving zakāh'. That is not necessary, since the agent with the maṣdar is omitted. It may be, in meaning, annexed to an omitted overt noun, including those to whom revelation was sent and others, the implied form being: 'the doing of good deeds by those under obligation'. It may also be annexed to the pronoun of those to whom revelation was sent, i.e. [that] they do good deeds, establish prayer and give zakāh; and if it was revealed to them, their followers follow their course in that and it does not follow that it is specific to them. Then the belief in making the maṣdar passive is disputed. al-Akhfash allowed it. The sound view is to prohibit it, so what al-Zamakhsharī chose is not the chosen view."

I say: what appears is that al-Zamakhsharī did not give this implied form for the reason the Shaykh mentioned, so as to be bound by what he said; rather he gave it because the very act, which is a meaning, issues from its agent not through revelation but through the revelation of words that indicate it. It is as if it were said: "We revealed this wording, namely that good deeds be done"; then he formed that infinitive particle with what follows into an indefinite maṣdar governing what follows, then made it a maṣdar annexed to its object.

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "al-Iqām is a maṣdar. In this there is room for objection." End. By "room for objection" Ibn ʿAṭiyya means that the maṣdar of afʿala is on the pattern ifʿāl. If the middle radical is sound it comes complete, like al-ikrām; if it is weak, one of the two alifs is omitted and a tāʾ marbūṭa is substituted for it, so one says iqāma. Since it was not said so, the stated objection arose. The Shaykh said: "What objection is there in this? Sībawayh has stated that it is a maṣdar in the sense of al-iqāma, even though most often it is al-iqāma with tāʾ, which is the regular form for the maṣdar of afʿala when its middle radical is weak. What made it good is that it is set against {وَإِيتَآءَ الزكاة}, which is without tāʾ, so a balance results between His sayings {وَإِقَامَ الصلاة وَإِيتَآءَ الزكاة}."

al-Zajjāj said: "The tāʾ was omitted from iqāma because the annexation is a compensation for it." This is the view of al-Farrāʾ, who claimed that the tāʾ is omitted for annexation, like the tanwīn. The full treatment of that has been given at the reading of those who read in Barāʾa {عُدَّةً ولكن كَرِهَ} [al-Tawba: 46].

semin-durr:74-74.t:
His saying: {وَلُوطاً آتَيْنَاهُ}: «لُوْطاً» is accusative by an implied verb that the overt verb after it explains; the implied form: "and We gave Lūṭ, We gave him"; so it is a case of ishtighāl (preoccupation). The accusative in the like of this is the preferred one; for that reason only it was read, because its clause is conjoined to a verbal clause, which is one of the factors of preference.

His saying: {مِنَ القرية}: that is, "from the people of". This is indicated by His saying after it: {إِنَّهُمْ كَانُواْ}, and likewise the attribution of the doing of vile deeds to it, the people being meant. The verification of this has already been given. al-Khabāʾith is an adjective of an omitted noun described, i.e. "which did vile deeds".

semin-durr:76-76.t:
His saying: {وَنُوحاً}: two views. The first: it is accusative by conjunction to «لُوْطاً», so it shares with it the governing verb «آتَيْنا», which is explained by the overt «آتيناه». Likewise {وَدَاوُودَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ} [verse 78]; the implied form: "and Nūḥ, We gave him judgement (ḥukm), and Dāwūd and Sulaymān, We gave them judgement". On this «إذ» is a badal from «نوحاً» and from «داود وسليمان», a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl). The verification of the like of this has already been given in Ṭāhā.

The second: it is accusative by an implied "remember", i.e. "remember Nūḥ, Dāwūd and Sulaymān", that is, remember their report and their story; on this «إذ» is accusative by the implied muḍāf itself, i.e. "their report, which took place at a time when such and such happened".

His saying: {مِن قَبْلُ}: that is, before these who were mentioned.

semin-durr:77-77.t:
His saying: {مِنَ القوم}: several views on it. The first: «نَصَرْناه» is made to include the meaning "We protected him and shielded him". Similar is {فَمَن يَنصُرُنَا مِن بَأْسِ الله} [Ghāfir: 29]; since it was made to include that meaning it became transitive as that is. The second: naṣara has the reflexive-reciprocal form intaṣara, so it takes the same construction as its counterpart. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is naṣara whose counterpart is intaṣara. I heard a Hudhalī praying against a thief: «اللهم انْصُرْهم منه», i.e. make them avengers against him (muntaṣirīn minhu)." No difference appears in relation to the inclusion mentioned; for the meaning of his saying "muntaṣirīn minhu" is "protected from him" or "shielded from him".

The third: «مِنْ» has the sense of «على», i.e. "against the people".

semin-durr:78-78.t: His saying: {لِحُكْمِهِمْ}: there are several aspects to the pronoun annexed to «حُكْم». The first: it is a pronoun by which the dual is meant, and the plural occurs in place of the dual figuratively, or because the dual is a plural and the minimum plural is two. That the dual is meant is indicated by the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās «لحُكْمِهما» in dual form. The second: the maṣdar is annexed to the two judges, who are Dāwūd and Sulaymān, and to the one judged for and the one judged against, and on this they are a group. This requires the maṣdar to be annexed to its agent and its object at once, whereas it is annexed to only one of them. It also combines the literal and the figurative, for the literal is the annexation of the maṣdar to its agent and the figurative its annexation to its object. The third: this maṣdar is not meant to indicate an action of labour but is brought to indicate that this event occurred and issued, as in their saying: "he has intelligence, the intelligence of the wise, and understanding, the understanding of the clever"; so it is not resolved into an infinitive particle and a verb, and when that is so it is annexed in meaning to the judge, the one judged for and the one judged against. The two objections mentioned are thereby removed.

semin-durr:79-79.t:
The majority read «فَفَهَّمْناها» with the doubling (shadda) that serves for transitivity; the pronoun refers to the question or to the legal opinion (fatyā). ʿIkrima read «فَأَفْهَمْناها» with a hamza, making it transitive by the hamza as the majority made it transitive by doubling.

His saying: {يُسَبِّحْنَ}: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. «الطيرَ» may be accusative by conjunction to «الجبالِ», or as a mafʿūl maʿahu. It was also said: «يُسَبِّحْن» is resumptive and has no position; this is remote. «والطيرُ» was also read in the nominative, and there are two views on it. One: it is a mubtadaʾ with its khabar omitted, i.e. "and the birds were also subjected". The other: it is conjoined to the pronoun in «يُسَبِّحْن» without emphasis or separator, which agrees with the Kufan school.

Al-Nafsh is spreading out, and from it is {كالعهن المنفوش} [al-Qāriʿa: 5]. «نَفَشَتِ الماشيةُ» means the livestock grazed at night without a herdsman, the opposite of al-hamal, which is grazing by day without a herdsman.

semin-durr:80-80.t:
His saying: {لَبُوسٍ}: the majority read with fatḥa on the lām, and it is the thing prepared for wearing. The poet said:

3355 - البَسْ لكلِّ حالةٍ لَبُوْسَها ... إمَّا نَعيمَها وإمَّا بُوْسَها
(Put on for every state its garment, either its ease or its hardship.)

«لُبُوْس» with ḍamma was also read, and then it is either the plural of lubs, the maṣdar standing in place of the passive participle, or not standing in its place; the first is closer. «لكم» may be attached to «عَلَّمْناه», or attached to «صَنْعَة», so said Abū al-Baqāʾ, and there is remoteness in this; or attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «لَبوس».

His saying: {لِتُحْصِنَكُمْ}: this is the lām of purpose (lām kay). There are several aspects regarding what it is attached to. The first: it is attached to «عَلَّمْناه». This is apparent on the last two views; on the third view it is problematic, because it would require two prepositions identical in wording and meaning to be attached to the same thing. The answer: it is made a badal from «لكم» by repeating the governing preposition, as in His saying {لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بالرحمن لِبُيُوتِهِمْ} [al-Zukhruf: 33], and it is a badal of inclusion, since the «أنْ» that makes the implied verb accusative is interpreted together with what it governs as a maṣdar. That maṣdar is a badal of the pronoun of address in «لكم», a badal of inclusion, the implied form being: "We taught him the craft of garments for your protection".

The second: it is attached to «صَنْعَةَ», on the sense that it is a badal from «لكم» as explained, and that according to Abū al-Baqāʾ, who attached «لكم» to «صَنْعَةَ». The third: it is attached to the "being established" to which «لكم» is attached if we make it an adjective of what precedes.

The two Ḥaramī readers (Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr), the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Abū ʿAmr read «ليُحْصِنَكم» with the yāʾ of two dots below. The agent is Allah the Exalted, and on this view there is a shift of person (iltifāt), since the pronoun of the first person preceded it in His saying {وَعَلَّمْنَاهُ}; or the agent is Dāwūd, or the teaching, or the garment. Ḥafṣ and Ibn ʿĀmir read with the tāʾ of two dots above. The agent is the craft, or the coat of mail (dirʿ), which is feminine, or the garment, because what is meant by it is what is worn, which is the coat of mail, and the coat of mail is feminine as given earlier. Abū Bakr read «لِنُحْصِنَكم» with a nūn, following «عَلَّمْناه». In these three readings the ḥāʾ is sākin and the ṣād is light.

al-Aʿmash read «لتُحَصِّنَكم», and likewise al-Fuqaymī from Abū ʿAmr, with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and shadda on the ṣād for intensity; except that al-Aʿmash has the tāʾ of two dots above and Abū ʿAmr the yāʾ of two dots below. What the agent is has already been given.

semin-durr:81-81.t:
His saying: {وَلِسُلَيْمَانَ الريح}: the majority read the accusative, i.e. "and We subjected the wind to Sulaymān", so it is accusative by an implied governing verb. Ibn Hurmuz, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim in one transmission, read the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the khabar being the preposition phrase before it. al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ read it in the plural and accusative; Abū Ḥaywa in the plural and nominative. The discussion of plural and singular has already been given in al-Baqara, and some of these read likewise in Sabaʾ; its explanation will come, Allah willing.

His saying: {عَاصِفَةً}: a ḥāl. The governing element for it, in the reading of those who read the accusative, is the implied «سَخَّرْنا», and in the reading of those who read the nominative, the "being established" to which the khabar is attached. One says: «عَصَفَتِ الريحُ تَعْصِفُ عَصْفاً وعُصُوفاً», and so it is ʿāṣif and ʿāṣifa. Asad say «أَعْصَفَتْ» with an alif, «تُعْصِفُ», and so it is muʿṣif and muʿṣifa.

«تَجْري» may be a second ḥāl, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «عاصفةً», so that they are two nested ḥāls. Some claimed that {التي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا} is an adjective of the wind and that in the verse there is a fronting and delaying, the implied form being: "the wind, which We blessed, to the land"; that is strained.

semin-durr:82-82.t:
His saying: {مَن يَغُوصُونَ}: it may be a relative noun or a described indefinite. On either reading, its position is either accusative by conjunction to «الريح», i.e. "and We subjected to him those who dive", or nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar in the preposition phrase before it. The pronoun is plural, following the sense of «مَنْ». What made that good is the earlier plural in His saying {الشياطين}; when the side of meaning was strengthened, it was observed. A parallel is the saying:

3356 - وإنَّ مِن النَّسْوان مَنْ هي روضةٌ ... تَهِيْجُ الرياضُ قبلَها وتَصُوْحُ
(Among women there is one who is a meadow, before whom the gardens wither and dry up.)

He observed the feminine because of the earlier «وإنَّ مِن النِّسْوانِ».

{دُونَ ذلك} is an adjective of «عَمَلاً».

semin-durr:83-83.t:
His saying: {وَأَيُّوبَ}: like His saying {وَنُوحاً} [verse 76] and what follows it. The majority read «أني» (with fatḥa), because the calling governs it by an implied preposition, i.e. "that I". ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read with kasra. The school of the Basrans is an implied "saying", i.e. "he called and said: Indeed I"; the school of the Kufans treats calling as saying.

al-Ḍurr with ḍamma is illness in the body, and with fatḥa it is harm in anything, so it is more general than the first.

semin-durr:84-84.t: His saying: {رَحْمَةً}: two views. The most apparent: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi. The second: it is a maṣdar of an implied verb, i.e. "We showed him mercy". {مِّنْ عِندِنَا} is an adjective of «رحمةً».

semin-durr:85-85.t: His saying: {وَذَا الكفل}: and {وَذَا النون} [verse 87] are conjoined to «أيوبَ». «ذا» means "possessor of". al-Kifl here is guarantee (kafāla); it is said that he guaranteed certain matters and fulfilled them.

semin-durr:87-87.t:
{وَذَا النون}: the whale (al-ḥūt); it is pluralised as nīnān, like ḥūt and ḥītān. He was so named because the whale swallowed him.

His saying: {مُغَاضِباً}: a ḥāl from the agent of «ذهب». The form mufāʿala here may carry its usual sense of mutual participation, i.e. he was angry with his people and they with him, when they did not believe at the start. In some commentaries: "angry with his Lord". If that is sound from someone whose saying is taken into account, then the lām (in «لربه») should be causal and not for making the verb transitive to the object, i.e. "on account of his Lord and His religion". It is also possible that it means "angry (ghaḍbān)", with no mutual participation, like ʿāqabtu and sāfartu.

The majority read «مُغاضِباً» as an active participle. Abū Sharaf read «مغاضَباً» with fatḥa on the ḍād, in the passive. So the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] reported it; and al-Zamakhsharī reported from Abū Sharaf «مُغْضَباً» without an alif, from «أَغْضَبْتَه», so he is muġḍab.

His saying: {أَن لَّن}: this «أَنْ» is the lightened one, and its subject is an omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). {لَّن نَّقْدِرَ} is the khabar. The separator is the negative particle. The meaning: "that We will not constrain him", on the pattern of His sayings {فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ} [al-Fajr: 16] and {وَمَن قُدِرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقُهُ} [al-Ṭalāq: 7].

The majority read «نَقْدِرَ» with the nūn of majesty (the royal "We"), with fatḥa and a light dāl. The object is omitted, i.e. "the directions and places". al-Zuhrī read it with ḍamma and shadda on the dāl. Ibn Abī Laylā, Abū Sharaf, al-Kalbī and Ḥumayd ibn Qays read «يُقْدَر» with ḍamma on the yāʾ of two dots below and fatḥa on a light dāl, in the passive. al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on a light dāl. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and al-Yamānī read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on a shadda-ed dāl. On these two readings the agent is a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted.

His saying: {أَن لاَّ إله إِلاَّ أَنتَ}: two views are allowed for «أَنْ». The first: it is the lightened form of the heavy «أنَّ», so its subject, as given, is omitted, and the negated clause after it is the khabar. The second: it is explicative (tafsīriyya), because it comes after what has the sense of saying, though not its letters.

semin-durr:88-88.t:
His saying: {وكذلك نُنجِي}: the kāf is an adjective of a maṣdar, or a ḥāl from the pronoun of the maṣdar. The majority read «نُنْجي» with ḍamma on the first nūn and sukūn on the second, from anjā yunjī. Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «نُجِّيْ» with shadda on the jīm and sukūn on the yāʾ. There are several aspects to it. The best: that the original is «نُنَجِّي», with ḍamma on the first (nūn), fatḥa on the second and shadda on the jīm; the succession of two identical letters was found heavy, so the second was omitted, as it was omitted in His saying {وَنُزِّلَ الملائكة} [al-Furqān: 25] in the reading of those who read it so, as given earlier, and as the second tāʾ was omitted in His saying {تَذَكَّرُونَ} [al-Anʿām: 152] and {تَظَاهَرُونَ} [al-Baqara: 85] and similar.

But Abū al-Baqāʾ considered this explanation weak on two grounds. He said: "One: the second nūn is original, being the fāʾ of the word, so its omission is very remote. The other: its vowel differs from the vowel of the first nūn, so the combination of the two is not found heavy, unlike «تَظاهَرون». Do you not see that if you said «تُتَحامى المظالِمُ», omitting the second would not be allowed?"

As for the second's being original, it has no effect in preventing omission. Do you not see that the grammarians differed over iqāma and istiqāma: which of the two alifs is omitted? Although the first is original, being the middle radical of the word. As for the difference of vowel, it too has no effect, because the heaviness arises from the sameness of the two letters in whatever vowel they occur.

The second aspect: «نُجِّي» is a passive past verb, and its lām was made sākin only for lightness, as it was made sākin in His saying {مَا بَقِيْ مِنَ الربا} [al-Baqara: 278] in an anomalous reading that has been given to you. They said: if the sound past was made sākin for lightness, the weak one is more fitting; and from it:

3357 - إنّما شِعْرِيَ قَيْدٌ ... قد خُلِطْ بجُلْجُلانِ
(My poetry is only a fetter that has been mixed with sesame seed.) [Translator's note: this gloss is tentative; the verse is cited for the sukūn on the final letter of the passive past «خُلِطْ».]

I have mentioned a good number of such cases.

This verb is attributed to the pronoun of the maṣdar even though a plain direct object exists, like the reading of Abū Jaʿfar {ليجزى قَوْماً بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكْسِبُونَ} [al-Jāthiya: 14]. This is the view of the Kufans and al-Akhfash. I have mentioned evidence for it earlier in this work; the implied form is: «نُجِّيَ النَّجاءُ» ("deliverance was delivered"). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is weak on two grounds: one, making the end of the past verb sākin; the other, letting the maṣdar stand in as deputy agent while a plain direct object exists." I say: you know the answer to both from what has preceded.
