The third aspect: the original is «ننجِّي» as in the reading of the majority, except that the second nūn was changed into a jīm and assimilated into the following jīm. This is very weak, because the nūn is not close to the jīm so as to be assimilated into it.

The fourth aspect: it is a past verb attributed to the pronoun of the maṣdar, i.e. «نُجِّي النَّجاءُ», as in the second aspect, except that «المؤمنين» is not accusative by «نجِّي» but by an implied verb. It seems that the proponent of this aspect fled from making something other than the direct object the deputy agent while the direct object exists, so he made it part of another clause.

This reading is mutawātir, and no attention is to be paid to one who attacked its reader, even if Abū ʿAlī said: "It is a solecism (laḥn)." That is a boldness on his part, which Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj preceded him in. As for al-Zamakhsharī, he did not attack it; he attacked only some of the aspects I presented earlier, saying: "Whoever strains for its soundness, making it fuʿila and saying «نُجِّي النَّجاءُ المؤمنين», dropping the yāʾ, attributing it to its maṣdar and making «المؤمنين» accusative, that is a strained effort, coldly strained." I say: he did not approve of this derivation, but for him the reading has another derivation. It may be the one I began with, for its being free of the weakness mentioned.

semin-durr:90-90.t:
His saying: {وَيَدْعُونَنَا}: the majority have the nūn of the nominative present, separate from the «نا». One group read «يَدْعُوْنا» with the nūn of the nominative omitted. Ṭalḥa read with it assimilated into it. In these two aspects the nūn of «نا» is treated like the protective nūn (nūn al-wiqāya). This has already been given.

His saying: {رَغَباً وَرَهَباً}: both may be accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi; or as two maṣdars standing in place of a ḥāl, i.e. "desiring and fearing"; or as a maṣdar that meets its governing verb in meaning but not in form, because that is a kind of it.

The majority read with fatḥa on the ghayn and the hāʾ. Ibn Wathāb and al-Aʿmash, and it is transmitted from Abū ʿAmr, read with sukūn on the ghayn and the hāʾ. It is reported from al-Aʿmash, and this is the better-known from him, with ḍamma on the rāʾ and on what follows. One group read with ḍamma and sukūn in both.

semin-durr:91-91.t:
His saying: {والتي أَحْصَنَتْ}: it may be accusative by conjunction to what precedes; it may be accusative by an implied "remember"; and it may be nominative as a mubtadaʾ with its khabar omitted, i.e. "and in what is recited to you is she who guarded". The khabar may also be «فنفَخْنا», with the fāʾ added in the view of al-Akhfash, like «زيدٌ فقائمٌ».

In the words of al-Zamakhsharī: «فَنَفَخْنا الروحَ في عيسى فيها». The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said, taking him to task: "He used «نَفَخَ» transitively. What is preserved is that it is not transitive, so it needs a report from the Arabs for its being transitive; and he used it intransitively in his saying «i.e. she blew into the flute»." End of his objection. I say: «نَفَخَ» has been heard as transitive. This is indicated by what was read in an anomalous reading, «فأنفخها فيكونُ طائراً», which he himself reported as a reading; how then does he deny it? Pay attention to that.

His saying: {آيَةً}: it does not agree with the first object, so that the second would be dualised, because each of the two is a sign through the other, so they became one sign. Or we say: it was omitted from the first because the second indicates it, or the reverse, i.e. "We made the son of Maryam a sign, and his mother likewise". It is a parallel to the omission in His saying {والله وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ} [al-Tawba: 62], which has already been given.

semin-durr:92-92.t:
His saying: {أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً}: the majority read the nominative «أمتكُم» as the khabar of «إنَّ», and the accusative «أمةً واحدةً» as a ḥāl. It was also said: as a badal from «هذه», in which case the khabar separates the badal from what it substitutes for, like «إن زيداً قائمٌ أخاك».

al-Ḥasan read «أُمَّتَكم» in the accusative, as a badal from «هذه» or as explicative apposition. He also read, together with Ibn Abī Isḥāq, al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī, Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Hārūn from Abū ʿAmr, «أُمَّتُكم أمَّةٌ واحدةٌ» with all three nominative, either with «أمتُكم» as the khabar of «إنَّ» as given earlier, and «أمةٌ واحدةٌ» a badal of it, an indefinite badal from a definite; or with «أمةٌ واحدةٌ» as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ.

semin-durr:93-93.t:
His saying: {أَمْرَهُمْ}: three views on it. The first: it is accusative by dropping the preposition, i.e. "they split up in their affair". The second: it is a direct object, and «تَقَطَّعوا» was made transitive because it has the sense of «قَطَّعوا». The third: it is a tamyīz. It is not clear in meaning, and it is definite, so it is not sound by the craft of the Basrans. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It was also said: it is a tamyīz, i.e. «تقطَّع أمرُهم»", making it transferred from the agent position.

«زُبُراً» may be a second object, on the basis that «تقطَّعوا» includes the sense "they turned, by cutting up"; or it may be accusative as a ḥāl from the object, i.e. "like zubur", that is, books, since al-zubur is the plural of zabūr like rusul, plural of rasūl; or it may be a ḥāl from the agent. Abū al-Baqāʾ reported this in Sūrat al-Muʾminūn. There is room for objection in it, as it has no sense; it appears as a ḥāl from the agent only in the reading «زُبَرا» with fatḥa on the bāʾ, i.e. "sects". The meaning: "they turned their affair into pieces" or "they cut it up in this state". The two views are taken from al-Zamakhsharī's explanation of the meaning of the noble verse, for he said: "The meaning: they made the affair of their religion among themselves into pieces, as a group distributes a thing and divides it among themselves, so that this one flies off with a share and that one with a share, as a likeness for their disagreement in it and their becoming sects and parties."

In the speech there is a shift (iltifāt) from address, namely «أمتُكم», to the third person, as an censure of them for their evil deed.

al-Aʿmash read with fatḥa on the bāʾ, the plural of zubra, which originally is a piece of iron. Its accusative is as a ḥāl from the pronoun of the agent in «تقطَّعوا»; this has already been given. Abū al-Baqāʾ did not deal with it in this sūra, but dealt with it in al-Muʾminūn, and mentioned in it the aspects given earlier, and added that «زُبْراً» was read with sukūn on the bāʾ, with the same sense as the ḍamma form.

semin-durr:94-94.t:
His saying: {فَلاَ كُفْرَانَ}: al-Kufrān is a maṣdar with the meaning of al-kufr. He said:

3358 - رأيتُ أُناساً لا تَنام جُدُوْدُهُمْ ... وجَدّيْ ولا كفرانَ لله نائمُ
(I saw people whose fortunes do not sleep, while my fortune sleeps — and there is no ingratitude toward Allah.)

«لِسَعْيه» is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "he is denied for his effort"; and it is not attached to «كفران», because it would then be a prolonged (muṭawwal) noun, and a prolonged noun is accusative; and this one is built (on fatḥa). The pronoun in «له» refers to the effort.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {اقترب لِلنَّاسِ}: the lām is attached to «اقترب». al-Zamakhsharī said: "This lām must be either a complement of «اقترب», or an emphasis of the annexation of the reckoning to them, as in your saying «أَزِفَ للحَيِّ رحيلُهم»: the original is «أَزِفَ رحيلُ الحيِّ», then «أَزِفَ للحيِّ الرحيلُ», then «أزف للحيِّ رحيلُهم». Like it is what Sībawayh adduced in the chapter 'what is repeated for emphasis in the case of the settled element', such as «عليك زيدٌ حريصٌ عليك» and «فيك زيد راغب فيك», and from it their saying «لا أبا لك», because the lām there emphasizes the meaning of annexation. This view is stranger than the first." The Shaykh said: "By his saying 'a complement of «اقترب»' he means attached to it. As for his making the lām an emphasis of the annexation of the reckoning to them, with the lām put first and entering an overt noun, we know of no one who says that. Also it would need something to attach to, and it cannot be attached to «حسابُهم», because that is a maṣdar with a connected object, since its dependent was put before it. Also emphasis comes after what is emphasized, and in this construction, were it delayed, it would not be valid. As for his likening it to what Sībawayh adduced, the difference is clear: «عليك» is dependent on «حريصٌ», and the later «عليك» is emphasis; likewise «فيك زيدٌ راغبٌ فيك», where «فيك» is attached to «راغبٌ» and the second «فيك» is emphasis. What misled him in that is the validity of the construction «حسابِ الناس», and likewise «أَزِفَ رحيلُ الحيِّ»; he supposed that when the overt noun is put before, genitive by the lām, and the maṣdar is annexed to its pronoun, it is of the type «فيك زيد راغب فيك», but it is not like it. As for «لا أبا لك», it is a problematic issue, with disagreement in it, and it may be said of it as he said, because the lām in it adjoins the annexation; but it is not to be used as a measure because of its irregularity and departure from the norms."
I say: the issue of al-Zamakhsharī is the most similar thing to the issue of «لا أبا لَك», and the meaning he gave is sound. As to its being problematic, he built that only on the saying of the majority, and the problematic one is established in its chapter, so measuring on it does not harm us, since it is established in its place.
His saying: {وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مُّعْرِضُونَ}: the preposition and its genitive noun may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مُعْرِضُون», or be a khabar of the pronoun, with «مُعْرِضون» a second khabar. The saying of Abū l-Baqāʾ about this prepositional phrase, "it is a second khabar", means in number, otherwise it is in truth the first. It might be said: since it is in the interpretation of a single word, the explicit single word was put first in rank, so it is second in this respect. This sentence is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from «للناس».

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {مُّحْدَثٍ}: The majority read «مُحْدَثٍ» genitive as an adjective of «ذِكْرٍ» by wording. His saying {مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ} has several views, the best being that it is attached to «يَأْتيهم», with «مِنْ» for the beginning of the range, figuratively. The second: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «مُحْدَثٍ». The third: that it is a ḥāl from «ذِكْرٍ» itself, though indefinite, because it has become specific by the description with «مُحْدَثٍ»; it is like «ما جاءني رجلٌ قائماً منطلقٌ», where the ḥāl separates the adjective from the described. Also the speech is a negation, which justifies a ḥāl from an indefinite. The fourth: that it is an adjective of «ذِكْر», so its position allows two views: genitive by wording, and nominative by position, because it is nominative in position since «مِنْ» is redundant in it, as will come. There is a problem in making it an adjective of «ذِكْرٍ», in that a non-explicit element is put before an explicit one; its treatment was given in al-Māʾida. The fifth: that it is attached to an omitted element by way of clarification.
Ibn Abī [ʿAbla] read «مُحْدَثٌ» nominative, an adjective of «ذِكْرٍ» by position, because «مِنْ» is redundant in it through the fulfilment of the two conditions. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "If it were nominative on the position of «مِنْ ذكْر» it would be permissible", as though he were unaware of it as a reading. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «مُحْدَثاً» accusative as a ḥāl from «ذِكْر»; what justifies that is its being described by «مِنْ ربِّهم» if we make it an adjective, or its depending on the negation. It may also be from the latent pronoun in «مِنْ ربهم» if we make it an adjective.
His saying: {إِلاَّ استمعوه}: this sentence is a ḥāl from the object of «يأتيهم»; it is a "voided" exception, and «قد» is implied with it according to some.
His saying: {وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ}: a ḥāl from the agent of «استمعوه».

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {لاَهِيَةً}: it may be a ḥāl from the agent of «اسْتَمَعوه» according to those who allow multiple ḥāls, the two ḥāls being successive; or a ḥāl from the agent of «يَلْعَبون», the two ḥāls being nested. al-Zamakhsharī expressed it saying: "{وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ لاَهِيَةً قُلُوبُهُمْ} are two ḥāls, successive or nested." If we make them two successive ḥāls, there is the putting of the non-explicit ḥāl before the explicit, which raises the same discussion as in the chapter on the adjective. «قلوبُهم» is nominative by «لاهِيَةً».
The majority read «لاهِيَةً» accusative. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it nominative as a second khabar of «وهم», according to those who allow that, or as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ according to those who do not allow it.
His saying: {وَأَسَرُّواْ النجوى الذين ظَلَمُواْ}: three views are allowed for the position of «الذين»: nominative, accusative and genitive. The nominative has several views. One: that it is a badal of the wāw of «أَسَرُّوا», to draw attention to their being marked with gross wrongdoing; Ibn ʿAṭiyya attributed it to Sībawayh, and others to al-Mubarrad.
The second: that it is the agent, and the wāw is a sign of plurality indicating the plural of the agent, as the tāʾ indicates its feminine, and likewise they do for the dual, saying «قاما أخواك». They recited: 3331 - «يَلُوْمونني في اشتراء النَّخي ... لِ أهلي فكلُّهُمُ أَلْوَمُ» (They blame me for buying the palms, my family, and every one of them is more blaming). This issue was discussed in al-Māʾida at the saying of the Exalted {ثُمَّ عَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ كَثِيرٌ مِّنْهُمْ} [verse 71], and al-Akhfash and Abū ʿUbayda held it. Some deemed this dialect weak, others deemed it good and ascribed it to Azd Shanūʾa; the issue was discussed in al-Māʾida at the saying of the Exalted {ثُمَّ عَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ كَثِيرٌ مِّنْهُمْ}.
The third: that «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ and «أَسَرُّوا» a predicative sentence put before the mubtadaʾ; this is attributed to al-Kisāʾī.
The fourth: that «الذين» is nominative by an implied verb, whose implied form is said to be "those who did wrong say". al-Naḥḥās preferred it, saying: "Saying is often implied. What indicates it is His saying afterward {هَلْ هاذآ إِلاَّ بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ}." It is also said: its implied form is «أَسَرَّها الذين ظلموا».
The fifth: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, implied as "they are those who did wrong".
The sixth: that it is a mubtadaʾ, with the sentence {هَلْ هاذآ إِلاَّ بَشَرٌ} as its khabar; on this view saying must be implied, as "Those who did wrong say: 'Is this but a human being?'", and saying is often implied.
The accusative has two views: one, blame (dhamm); the second, an implied «أعني» ('I mean'). The genitive also has two views: one, an adjective, and the other a badal, of «للناس»; this is attributed to al-Farrāʾ, and there is remoteness in it.
His saying: {هَلْ هاذآ} to His saying {تُبْصِرُونَ}: these two interrogative sentences may be in the position of accusative as a badal of «النجوى», or in the position of accusative by implied saying; al-Zamakhsharī said both. They may also be in the position of accusative as quoted by «النجوى», because it has the sense of saying. {وَأَنتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ} is a ḥāl sentence from the agent of «تَأْتُون».

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {قُلْ رَبِّي}: The two brothers and Ḥafṣ read «قال» in the wording of a report; the pronoun refers to the Messenger, peace be upon him. The rest read «قُلْ» as a command addressed to him.
His saying: {فِي السمآء}: several views. One: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl of «القول». The second: that it is a ḥāl of the agent of «يعلمُ»; Abū l-Baqāʾ judged it weak, and it should be barred. The third: that it is attached to «يَعْلَمُ», which is close to the one before it. The complement of «السميع العليم» is omitted because it is known.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلاَمٍ}: the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is muddled dreams". The sentence is accusative by «القول».
His saying: {كَمَآ أُرْسِلَ}: two views for this kāf. One: that it is in the position of genitive as an adjective of «آيةٍ», i.e. "with a sign like the sign of the sending of the earlier ones"; «ما» is then a maṣdar particle. The second: that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a coming like the sending of the earlier ones".

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {أَهْلَكْنَاهَآ} and {أَفَهُمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ}: the like of it has been discussed.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {نوحي إِلَيْهِمْ}: Ḥafṣ read «نُوْحي» with the nūn of majesty, in the active, i.e. "We reveal". The rest read it with the yāʾ and fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, in the passive; that was discussed in Yūsuf. This sentence is in the position of accusative as an adjective of «رِجالاً»; and «إليهم», in the first reading, is accusative in position, and the object is omitted, i.e. "We reveal to them the Qurʾān" or "the Reminder"; in the second reading it is nominative in position because it stands in place of the agent.
His saying: {إِن كُنتُمْ لاَ تَعْلَمُونَ}: the apodosis of the condition is omitted because what precedes it indicates it, i.e. «فاسْأَلوهم» ('ask them'). The two objects of «العلم» may be intended, i.e. "you do not know that this is so", or may not be intended, i.e. "if you are of those without knowledge".

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {لاَّ يَأْكُلُونَ الطعام}: two views on this sentence. The clearer: that it is in the position of accusative as an adjective of «جَسَداً», and «جَسَداً» is singular meant as plural, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "possessors of bodies not eating food". This is a rebuttal of their saying {مَالِ هذا الرسول يَأْكُلُ الطعام} [al-Furqān: 7]. «جعل» may mean «صَيَّر», taking two objects, the second being «جسداً»; or it may mean «خلق» and «أنشأ», taking one, in which case «جسداً» is a ḥāl by interpreting it as a derived word, i.e. "nourished", because a body needs nourishment.
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«لا يأكلون» is another ḥāl after «جَسَداً» if we say that «جعل» takes one object." There is room for objection in it; rather it is an adjective of «جَسَداً» on both considerations, and only that suits the meaning.

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {صَدَقْنَاهُمُ الوعد}: «صَدَق» takes two objects, the second with a preposition, which may be omitted. You say «صَدَقْتُك الحديثَ», and in the ḥadīth. The like: «أمر» and «استغفر»; it has been discussed in Āl ʿImrān. [Translator's note: the source sentence is garbled: «وفي الحديث. نحو: أمر واستغفر», with no ḥadīth quoted; translated as written.]

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ}: it may be a sentence in the position of accusative as an adjective of «كتاباً», or «فيه» alone may be the description and «ذِكْرُكم» the agent. Some said: "In the speech there is an omitted muḍāf, implied as: 'in it is mention of your honour.'" «ذِكْر» here is a maṣdar that may be annexed to its object, i.e. "Our mentioning you"; or annexed to its agent, i.e. "what you mentioned of idolatry and the denial of the Prophet ﷺ".

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {وَكَمْ قَصَمْنَا}: in the position of accusative as a fronted object of «قَصَمْنا». «من قرية» is a tamyīz. The apparent view is that «كم» here is informative (khabariyya), because it gives the sense of multiplicity.
His saying: {كَانَتْ ظَالِمَةً}: in the position of genitive as an adjective of «قريةٍ». An omitted muḍāf is needed before «قرية», i.e. "how many people of a town We shattered", by the evidence of the pronoun's return in His saying {فلمَّا أحَسُّوا}; it cannot refer to His saying «قوماً», because nothing was mentioned of them that would require that.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {إِذَا}: this is the «إذا» of suddenness (fujāʾiyya). The disagreement about it has been discussed at length. «هم» is a mubtadaʾ and «يَرْكُضون» its khabar. It was said at the beginning of this topic that this verse and its like indicate that «لَمَّا» is not temporal but a particle of "occurrence for occurrence", because a temporal adverb needs a governing element and there is none here, since what follows «إذا» does not govern what precedes it. The answer: the sense of suddenness, indicated by «إذا», governed in it.
The pronoun in «مِنْها» refers to «قرية». It may refer to «بَأْسَنا», because it has the sense of vengeance and affliction, so the pronoun was made feminine by carrying it over to the meaning. «مِنْ» on the first is for the beginning of the range, and on the second for cause. «الرَّكْض» is striking the beast with the foot. It is said «رَكَضَ الدابَّةَ يَرْكُضها رَكْضاً».

semin-durr:95-95.t:
His saying: {وَحَرَامٌ}: the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Abū Bakr read, and it is also transmitted from Abū ʿAmr, «وحِرْمٌ» with kasra on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the rāʾ. They are two dialect forms, like al-ḥill and al-ḥalāl. Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿIkrima read «حَرِمَ» with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, kasra on the rāʾ and fatḥa on the mīm, as a past verb. It is also transmitted from them both, and from Abū al-ʿĀliya, with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and the mīm and ḍamma on the rāʾ, on the pattern of karuma, also a past verb. From Ibn ʿAbbās there is also the reading with fatḥa on all, again a past verb. al-Yamānī read with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, shadda-ed kasra on the rāʾ and fatḥa on the mīm, a passive past. From ʿIkrima it is transmitted with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, kasra on the rāʾ and tanwīn on the mīm.

For one who takes it as a noun, there are two views on its being nominative. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar then has three aspects. The first: His saying {أَنَّهُمْ لاَ يَرْجِعُونَ}, and in that there are four interpretations. The first interpretation: «لا» is redundant and the meaning is: "it is impossible for a town whose destruction We decreed because of their disbelief that they return to faith, until the Hour comes". Abū ʿAmr took the view of its redundancy, citing as evidence His saying {مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلاَّ تَسْجُدَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 12], in one of the two views. The second interpretation: it is not redundant, and the meaning is that they will not turn back from their disobedience and disbelief. The third interpretation: "forbidden" (ḥarām) is meant as "obligatory". This is indicated by His saying {قُلْ تَعَالَوْاْ أَتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَلاَّ تُشْرِكُواْ} [al-Anʿām: 151], and abandoning association is obligatory; it is also indicated by the saying of al-Khansāʾ:

3359 - حرامٌ عليَّ لا أرى الدهرَ باكياً ... على شَجْوِه إلا بَكَيْتُ على صَخْرِ
(It is forbidden for me that I should ever see anyone weeping over his grief without my weeping over Ṣakhr.)

Moreover, it is part of usage to apply one of two opposites to the other. Hence al-Ḥasan and al-Suddī said: "They will not return from association." Qatāda said: "to the world." The fourth interpretation: Abū Muslim ibn Baḥr said: "Ḥarām means impossible. And «أنهم لا يرجعون» is the negation of return to the Hereafter; so when the negation is impossible, return is obligatory. The meaning: their return to life in the Abode of the Hereafter is obligatory. The aim would be to refute the saying of those who deny the resurrection, and to verify what preceded, that there is no ingratitude toward anyone's effort and that he will be recompensed for it on the Day of Resurrection." The saying of Ibn ʿAṭiyya is close to this; he said: "It is impossible for the destroyed disbelievers that they not return to Allah's punishment and His painful retribution; so «لا» is in its usual sense and ḥarām in its usual sense."

The second aspect (of the khabar): the khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "their repentance is forbidden" or "hope for their resurrection", and «أنَّهم لا يَرْجعون» would be the reason for the meaning of the preceding sentence; but then you have two possibilities for «لا». The first possibility: that it is redundant. For that reason Abū al-Baqāʾ said, in this view after giving the aforementioned implied khabar: "if you make «لا» redundant". I say: the meaning for him is: "because they return to the Hereafter and its recompense". The second possibility: that it is not redundant, meaning: "their repentance, or hope for their resurrection, is impossible, because they will not return to the world to make up in it what they missed of that".

The third aspect: this mubtadaʾ has no khabar, neither in wording nor in implication, but it takes a nominative that stands in the place of its khabar, on the pattern of «أقائم أخواك؟». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The good view is that «أنهم» is an agent standing in for the khabar." I say: there is room for objection in this, because it is a condition there that the descriptive depend on a negation or an interrogative, and here the mubtadaʾ does not depend on either; unless he takes the line of al-Akhfash, who does not require that. I have set out this question elsewhere, and what appears is the position of al-Akhfash. In that case «لا» has the two earlier aspects, of redundancy and non-redundancy, with two different meanings: that is, "their return to the world, or from their association, is impossible" if you take it as redundant, or "their not returning to Allah's punishment in the Hereafter is impossible" if you take it as non-redundant.

The second of the two views on the nominative of «حرام»: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. Some gave the implied form: "pardon and repentance are forbidden". Abū al-Baqāʾ gave it as: "that is, that which was mentioned of righteous deed is forbidden". al-Zamakhsharī said: "«وحرامٌ على قريةٍ أهلكناها ذَاك», and it is what was mentioned in the preceding verse of righteous deeds and thanked effort, not denied. Then he gave a reason, saying: they will not return from disbelief, so how could that not be impossible?"

The majority read «أَهْلكناها» with the nūn of majesty. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Qatāda read «أهلكتُها» with the tāʾ of the speaker. Whoever read «حَرِمٌ» with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, kasra on the rāʾ and tanwīn on the mīm, in his reading it is an adjective on the pattern faʿil, like ḥadhir. He said:

3360 - وإن أتاه خليلٌ يومَ مسألةٍ ... يقولُ لا غائبٌ مالي ولا حَرِمُ
(And if a friend came to him on a day of asking, he says: my wealth is neither absent nor forbidden.)

And whoever read it as a past verb, in his reading it is attributed to «أنَّ» and what is in its scope. The discussion of «لا» with regard to redundancy and non-redundancy is not obscure, for the meaning is clear from what has preceded. «إنَّهم» with kasra was also read, as resumptive, and then an implied mubtadaʾ is necessary to complete the speech, its implied form being: "that righteous deed is forbidden". The verification of that has been given.

semin-durr:96-96.t:
His saying: {حتى إِذَا}: the discussion of «حتى» entering upon «إذا» has already been given in full. al-Zamakhsharī said here: "If you say: what is «حتى» attached to, as it occurs as a limit for it, and which of the three is it? I say: it is attached to «حرامٌ» and is a limit for it, because the impossibility of their return does not end until the Resurrection comes; and it is the «حتى» after which speech is quoted, the quoted speech being the sentence of the condition and apodosis, I mean «إذا» and what is in its scope." Abū al-Baqāʾ took this line, saying: "«حتى» is attached in meaning to «حرامٌ», i.e. the impossibility continues until this time, and it has no effect on «إذا»."

al-Ḥūfī said: "It is a limit, and what governs it is what the meaning indicates, namely their regret over what they neglected of obedience when it was too late to make up for it." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«حتى» is attached to His saying «وتَقَطَّعوا». On some of the interpretations given earlier it may be attached to «يَرْجِعون», and it may be a particle of commencement, which is the most apparent, because of «إذا»; for it requires an apodosis which is what is meant to be mentioned." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "The attachment of «حتى» to «تَقَطَّعوا» is remote because of the many separators, but in meaning it is good: namely that they will continue to differ about the religion of truth until near the coming of the Hour, and when the Hour comes all that ceases."

In summary, concerning what «حتى» is attached to there are several aspects. The first: it is attached to «حرامٌ». The second: it is attached to an omitted element that the meaning indicates, which is al-Ḥūfī's view. The third: it is attached to «تَقَطَّعوا». The fourth: it is attached to «يَرْجِعون». In summary, concerning «حتى» itself there are two views: one, it is a particle of commencement, which is the view of al-Zamakhsharī and, in what he chose, Ibn ʿAṭiyya; two, a preposition meaning «إلى».

Ibn ʿĀmir read «فُتِّحَتْ» with shadda; the others read it light. This was given at the beginning of al-Anʿām. There are several aspects regarding the apodosis of «إذا». The first: it is omitted. Abū Isḥāq gave the implied form: "they said: Woe to us", while others gave: "then at that moment they will be resurrected". And His saying «فإذا هي شاخصة» is conjoined to this implied element. The second: its apodosis is the fāʾ in His saying «فإذا هي»; so said al-Ḥūfī, al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya. al-Zamakhsharī said: "«إذا» in «فإذا هي» is the «إذا» of surprise, and it occurs in recompense standing in the place of the fāʾ, as in His saying {إِذَا هُمْ يَقْنَطُونَ} [al-Rūm: 36]; so when the fāʾ comes with it, the two cooperate in linking the recompense to the condition, which makes it emphatic. Had it been said «إذا هي شاخصة» it would have been sound." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "What I say is that the apodosis is in His saying «فإذا هي شاخِصَةٌ»; and that is the meaning it is intended to mention, because it is their return, which they used to deny and whose impossibility was forbidden to them."

His saying: {يَأْجُوجُ}: this is with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the barrier of Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj". The discussion of the two has been given recently.

His saying «وهم» may refer to Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj, and it may refer to the whole world. The first is more apparent.

The majority read «يَنْسِلون» with kasra on the sīn; Abū al-Sammāl and Ibn Abī Isḥāq with ḍamma. Al-Ḥadab is the raised ground, that is, the elevated; from it al-ḥadab in the back (hump); and every hillock or mound is a ḥadaba, and the grave was named by it because of its rising above the surface of the ground. Al-Nasalān is short steps with speed. One says nasala yansilu and yansulu, with fatḥa in the past and kasra and ḍamma in the imperfect; and nasala and ʿasala are the same. The poet said:

3361 - عَسَلانَ الذئبِ أمسى قارِباً ... بَرَدَ الليلُ عليه فَنَسَلْ
(Like the trotting of the wolf who came near by evening; the night turned cold upon him, so he went trotting on.)

and al-nasl, which is offspring, is from this, the maṣdar applied to the passive participle. «نَسَلْتُ ريشَ الطائر» ("I plucked the feathers of the bird") is also from this. The prepositional phrase was put before what it is attached to for the harmony of the verse endings. ʿAbd Allāh and Ibn ʿAbbās read «جَدَث» with the three-dotted thāʾ, which means the grave. It was also read with fāʾ, which is a substitute for it. al-Zamakhsharī said: "The thāʾ is of the Hijāz and the fāʾ of Tamīm." It should be that both are originals, because each is an independent dialect; but replacing thāʾ with fāʾ is frequent. They said «مَعْثُور» for «مَعْفور», and they said «فُمَّ» for «ثُمَّ», so this was replaced by that at one time and that by this at another.

semin-durr:97-97.t:
His saying: {فَإِذَا هِيَ شَاخِصَةٌ أَبْصَارُ}: several aspects. The first, and it is the best: «هي» is the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa), «شاخصةٌ» is a fronted khabar, «أبصارُ» is a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of «هي», because it is explained only by a clause whose two parts are explicit; this is the school of the Basrans. The second: «شاخصة» is a mubtadaʾ and «أبصارُ» is an agent standing in for the khabar; this goes along with the view of the Kufans, because for them the pronoun of the story may be explained by a single word that works like a verb, since it is equivalent to a sentence. The third: al-Zamakhsharī said: «هي» is a vague pronoun which the "sights" (al-abṣār) clarify and explain, as {الذين ظَلَمُواْ} {وَأَسَرُّواْ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 3] explains. He mentioned nothing else. I say: this is the view of al-Farrāʾ, for he said: «هي» is the pronoun of the sights, put first because the speech indicates it and what explains it comes. He recited as evidence for that:

3362 - فلا وأبيها لا تقول حَليلتي ... ألا فَرَّعني مالكُ بنُ أبي كعبِ
(No, by her father — my wife will not say: "Ah, Mālik ibn Abī Kaʿb has overtopped me!") [Translator's note: the gloss of «فَرَّعني» is tentative.]

The fourth: «هي» is an ʿimād (supporting pronoun), which is also the view of al-Farrāʾ; he said: "because «هو» can take its place." He recited:

3363 - بثوبٍ ودينارٍ وشاةٍ ودِرْهمٍ ... فهل هو مرفوعٌ بما ههنا راسُ
(With a garment, a dinar, a sheep and a dirham — is it then lifted up by what is here, a head?) [Translator's note: the gloss is tentative; the verse is obscure.]

This goes along only with one of the two views of al-Kisāʾī, namely that he allows the fronting of the separator together with the fronted khabar, like «هو خيرٌ منك زيد», the original being: «زيدٌ هو خيرٌ منك». The Shaykh said: "He allowed «هو القائمُ زيدٌ», on the basis that «زيداً» is the mubtadaʾ, «القائم» its khabar and «هو» the ʿimād; and the original of the question is: «زيدٌ هو القائم»." I say: in this example there is [room for objection], because fronting the khabar here is impossible, for the two are equal in definiteness, unlike the example I gave earlier; so the original of the noble verse would be: «فإذا أبصارُ الذين كفروا هي شاخصةٌ»; when the khabar «شاخصةٌ» was fronted, the ʿimād was fronted with it. This too is acceptable only on the view of one who sees the ʿimād as occurring before an indefinite that is not near to a definite.

The fifth: «هي» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is implied, and the speech is then complete at «هي», and one begins anew with His saying «شاخصة أبصار». The implied form: "and behold it is manifest", i.e. the Hour is manifest or present; «شاخصةٌ» is a fronted khabar and «أبصارُ» a delayed mubtadaʾ. al-Thaʿlabī mentioned it. It is very remote because of the discordance of the construction, which is ʿtaʿqīd (convolution) in the view of the scholars of rhetoric.

His saying: {ياويلنا}: governed by an omitted saying, and concerning this omitted saying there are two views. The first: it is the apodosis of «حتى إذا», as given earlier. The second: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from «الذين كفروا»; so said al-Zamakhsharī.

semin-durr:98-98.t:
His saying: {وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ}: «ما», which is for the non-rational, is used here, because whenever the rational is mixed with others, the speaker may choose between «ما» and «مَنْ».

The majority read «حَصَبُ» with the two unpointed letters and fatḥa on the ṣād; it is what is hurled (yuḥṣabu), that is, thrown into the fire; and it is not called ḥaṣab except while it is in the fire. Before that it is firewood (ḥaṭab), trees and the like. It was also said: it is an Abyssinian word. It was also said: it is called ḥaṣab before being thrown into the fire. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read, and it is also transmitted from Ibn Kathīr, with sukūn on the ṣād; it is a maṣdar, which may stand in for the passive participle, or be for exaggeration, or be with an omitted muḍāf. Ibn ʿAbbās read it with the pointed ḍād, fatḥa or sukūn, which is likewise what is thrown into the fire; from it is al-miḥḍab, a stick with which the fire is stirred so that it blazes. It was recited:

3364 - فلا تَكُ في حَرْبِنا مِحْضَباً ... فتجعلَ قومَك شَتَّى شُعوبا
(Do not be a stirrer in our war, making your people scattered, divided tribes.)

The Commander of the Faithful (ʿAlī), Ubayy, ʿĀʾisha and Ibn al-Zubayr read «حَطَبُ» with ṭāʾ; I think it is only an explanation, not a recitation.

semin-durr:99-99.t:
His saying: {آلِهَةً}: the majority read the accusative, as the khabar of «كان». Ṭalḥa read it in the nominative. Its derivation is like that of the saying:

3365 - إذا مِتُّ كان الناسُ صِنْفَانِ. . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(When I die, the people will be two kinds ... [the rest elided in the source].)

in which there is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).

His saying: {أَنتُمْ لَهَا وَارِدُونَ}: Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed three aspects for this clause. The first: it is a badal from «حَصَبُ جنهم». I say: he means the clause is a badal from the single word that occurs as khabar, and substituting a clause for a single word is permitted when one has the sense of the other, since the implied form is: "You are those who come to it." The second: the clause is resumptive. The third: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from «جهنم»; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it. There is room for objection in it, in that a ḥāl comes from a muḍāf ilayhi outside the excepted cases.

semin-durr:101-101.t: His saying: {مِّنَّا}: it may be attached to «سَبَقَتْ», and it may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «الحسنى».

semin-durr:102-102.t:
His saying: {لاَ يَسْمَعُونَ}: it may be a badal from «مُبْعَدُون» because it takes its place and so suffices in its stead; it may be a second khabar; and it may be a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «مُبْعَدون».

His saying: {وَهُمْ فِي مَا اشتهت} up to «وتَتَلقَّاهم»: each clause of these clauses may be a ḥāl from what precedes it, and may be resumptive. Likewise the implied clause of saying, which governs the clause of His saying «هذا يومُكم», since the implied form is: "and they meet them, saying: this is your day".

semin-durr:104-104.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ نَطْوِي}: several aspects. The first: it is accusative by «لا يَحْزُنُهم». The second: it is accusative by «تتلقَّاهم». The third: it is accusative by an implied "remember" or "I mean". The fourth: it is a badal from the implied returning pronoun, its implied form being: "that which you are promised on the day We fold up"; so «يومَ» is a badal from the hāʾ. Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it. There is room for objection in it, since it requires the clause attached to the relative to be devoid of a returning pronoun referring to the relative; for that reason they prohibited «جاء الذي مررتُ به أبي عبد الله» on the basis that «أبي عبد الله» be a badal from the hāʾ, for the reason I mentioned, even though there is disagreement on the question. The fifth: it is accusative by «الفزع» (the terror); so said al-Zamakhsharī, and there is room for objection in it, in that he made the described maṣdar work before taking its object.

It has already been given that Nāfiʿ reads «يُحْزِنُ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ except here, and that his teacher Ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ reads «يَحْزُن» with fatḥa except here.

The majority read «نَطْوي» with the nūn of majesty, and Shayba ibn Niṣāḥ among others read «يطوي» with the third-person yāʾ, the agent being Allah the Exalted; and Abū Jaʿfar among others read «تطوى» with ḍamma on the tāʾ of two dots above and fatḥa on the wāw, in the passive.

The majority read «السِّجِلِّ» with kasra on the sīn and the jīm and shadda on the lām, like al-ṭimirr. Abū Hurayra and his companion Abū Zurʿa ibn ʿAmr ibn Jarīr read with ḍamma on both, the lām also with shadda, on the pattern of «عُتُلّ». Abū al-Baqāʾ also reported lightening of it in this reading, so that it is on the pattern of ʿunuq. Abū al-Sammāl, Ṭalḥa and al-Aʿmash read with fatḥa on the sīn; al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar [with kasra]. In these two readings the jīm is sākin and the lām light. Abū ʿAmr said: "The reading of the people of Mecca is like the reading of al-Ḥasan."

al-Sijill is the sheet (ṣaḥīfa) in general. It was also said that it is specific to a sheet of covenant; it is from al-musājala, and al-sajl is the full bucket. Some said: it is a Persian loan word, so it has no derivation.

«طَيّ» is a maṣdar annexed to the object. The agent is omitted, its implied form being: "as a man folds the sheet in order to write in it", or for what he writes in it of meanings; and the agent is regularly omitted with the maṣdar. The discussion of the kāf is well known, I mean its being an adjective of an implied maṣdar or a ḥāl from its pronoun. The original of ṭayy is ṭawy, which underwent weakening-change like its parallels.

It was also said: al-Sijill is the name of an angel who folds the records of the deeds of the children of Ādam. It was also said: the name of a man who used to write for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. On these two views the maṣdar is annexed to its agent. «الكتاب» is a name for the sheet written in. Abū Isḥāq said: "al-Sijill: the man, in the language of the Abyssinians." al-Zamakhsharī said: "As the scroll (al-ṭūmār) is folded for writing, that is, in order to be written in, or for what is written in it; because al-kitāb is originally a maṣdar like al-bināʾ, then is applied to what is written." So al-Zamakhsharī gave the implied form from the passive verb. You already know the disagreement in it.

The lām in «للكتاب» is either added to the object, if we say the maṣdar is annexed to its agent, or attached to ṭayy, or has the sense of «على». The last should not be permitted, given its remoteness in meaning on every view. The readings mentioned for «السِّجِلْ» are all dialect forms. The two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ḥafṣ read «للكتب» in the plural, and the others «للكتاب» in the singular; the script allows both: the singular means the genus, and the plural indicates the variety.

His saying: {كَمَا بَدَأْنَآ}: there are two views on what this kāf is attached to. The first: it is attached to «نُعِيده», and «ما» is a maṣdar particle and «بدأنا» its ṣila, so it and what is in its scope are in the position of genitive by the kāf. «أولَ خَلْقٍ» is the object of «بَدَأْنا». The meaning: "We shall restore the first creation, a restoring like Our beginning of it", that is, as We brought it out from non-existence into existence, We restore it from non-existence into existence. Abū al-Baqāʾ took this line, saying: "The kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. We restore it a return like its beginning." In his saying "a return (ʿawd)" there is room for objection, since it is better to say "restoration (iʿāda)".

The second: it is attached to an implied verb. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Another aspect: the kāf is accusative by an implied verb which «نُعيده» explains, and «ما» is a relative, i.e. «We restore the like of that which We began, We restore it»; «أولَ خَلْقٍ» is a ẓarf for «بَدَأْناه», i.e. the first thing He created, or a ḥāl from the pronoun of the relative, which is dropped from the wording but present in the meaning."

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "In his implication there is a preparing of «بَدَأْنا» to make «أولَ خَلْقٍ» accusative as an object and then cutting it off from it, without a necessity that calls for that, and he commits an implied element that is remote, explained by «نُعِيْدُه»; this is a non-Arabic quality (ʿujma) in the Book of Allah. As for his saying «another aspect: the kāf is accusative by an implied verb which «نُعِيدُه» explains», it is very weak, because it is built on the kāf being a noun, not a particle, and that is not the view of the majority; al-Akhfash alone took it. And its being a noun, for the Basrans, is restricted to poetry." I say: everything he implied runs on regulated rules and the sound meaning led him to it, so there is no fault in him. This is apparent upon reflection to anyone who is not obtuse.

As for his saying «ما», it has three aspects. The first: it is a maṣdar particle. The second: it has the sense of «الذي». The explanation of these two has been given. The third: it is a kāffa (restrainer) that stops the kāf from working, as in the saying:

3366 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كما الناسُ مَجْرُوْمٌ عليه وجارِمُ
(... as people are: one offended against and one who offends.) [The first half of the verse is elided in the source.]

for one who made «الناس» nominative. al-Zamakhsharī said: "«أولَ خَلْقٍ» is the object of «نُعيد», which «نُعِيده» explains, and the kāf is restrained by «ما». The meaning: We restore the first creation as We began it, likening the restoration to the beginning in that power embraces both equally. If you say: what is the first creation that He should restore it as He began it? I say: its first is its bringing into existence from non-existence; so as He brought it into existence first from non-existence, He restores it a second time from non-existence."

As for «أولَ خلق», four aspects result for it. The first: it is the object of «بَدَأْنا». The second: it is a ẓarf for «بَدَأْنا». The third: it is accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun of the relative, as all this was set out earlier. The fourth: it is a ḥāl from the object of «نُعيده»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said it, and the meaning: "like the first of its creation".

As for the indefiniteness of «خَلْقِ», it is to indicate detail; al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why is «خَلْقٍ» indefinite? I say: it is like your saying «هو أولُ رجلٍ جاءني» ('he is the first man who came to me'), meaning the first of the men; but you made it singular and indefinite, intending to detail them man by man. Likewise the meaning of «أولَ خَلْقٍ» is 'the first of creatures'; because al-khalq is a maṣdar and is not pluralised."

His saying: {وَعْداً}: accusative as a confirming maṣdar of the content of the preceding sentence, so what governs it is implied, i.e. "We promised that a promise".

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {فَمَا زَالَت تِلْكَ دَعْوَاهُمْ}: the ism of «زالَتْ» is «تلك» and «دعواهم» is the khabar; this is the correct view. al-Ḥūfī, al-Zamakhsharī and Abū l-Baqāʾ said the reverse is permissible. It is rejected on the ground that when the iʿrāb is hidden, while the two are equal in the justification for each being ism or khabar, the earlier must be made the ism and the later the khabar, as in «ضرب موسى عيسى»; the clarification of this was given at the beginning of Sūrat al-Aʿrāf. There is a point there that does not arise here, so pay attention to it. «تلك» points to the quoted sentence.
His saying: {حَصِيداً}: a second object, because «الجعل» here is making into (taṣyīr). {حَصِيداً خَامِدِينَ}: it may be of the type «هذا حلوٌ حامِضٌ» ('this is sweet-sour'), as though it were said: "We made them combine both descriptions". «خامِدِيْن» may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «جَعَلْناهم», or from the latent pronoun in «حَصِيداً», for it has the meaning of «مَحْصود». It may be of the type with multiple khabars, like «زيدٌ كاتبٌ شاعرٌ». Abū l-Baqāʾ also allowed that it be an adjective of «حَصيداً», with «حَصِيد» meaning «مَحْصود» as already said, and for that reason it was not pluralized. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The implied form: 'like a harvested thing', and for that reason it was not pluralized, as «مثل» in the implied is not pluralized." End. When it has the meaning of «مَحْصُودين» there is no need.

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {لاَعِبِينَ}: a ḥāl from the agent of «خَلَقْنا».

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {إِن كُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ}: two views about this «إنْ». One: that it is negative, i.e. "We were not doers". The second: that it is conditional, the apodosis omitted because the apodosis of «لو» indicates it; the implied form: "if We were doers, We would have taken it".

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {فَيَدْمَغُهُ}: The majority read the ghayn nominative, as a conjunction on what precedes. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read it accusative. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is as weak as the saying: 3332 - «سأَتْركُ منزلي لبني تميمٍ ... وألحقُ بالحجازِ فَأَسْتَريحا» (I shall leave my house to Banū Tamīm and join the Ḥijāz, and so rest)." «فيَدْمُغُه» with ḍamma on the mīm has been read irregularly; it allows that the imperfect has two forms, «يَفْعَلُ» and «يَفْعُل», or that the original is fatḥa and the ḍamma is for harmony with the guttural letter. «يدمغه» means it strikes his brain (dimāgh), from their saying «دَمَغْتُ الرجلَ», i.e. I struck him on the brain, like their saying «رَأَسَه», «كَبَده» and «رَجَله», when one strikes these organs of him.
His saying: {مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ}: several views. One: that it is attached to the "abiding" to which the khabar is attached, i.e. "woe abides for you on account of what you describe"; «مِنْ» is causal. This is a sound view. The second: that it is attached to an omitted element. The third: that it is a ḥāl from «الويل», i.e. "woe occurring because of what you describe"; so Abū l-Baqāʾ implied it. «ما» in {مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ} may be a maṣdar particle, so there is no returning pronoun according to the majority; or it may mean «الذي», or be an indefinite described one, in which case a returning pronoun is needed according to all, and it was omitted because the conditions are fulfilled.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ}: two views are allowed. One: that it is conjoined to the first «مَنْ». The Exalted reports about those in the heavens and the earth, and about those with Him, that all belong to Him in His dominion; on this it is of the type of mentioning the specific after the general, to draw attention to its honour, because His saying {مَن فِي السماوات} included those with Him. A parallel has passed in His saying {وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ} [al-Baqara: 98]. His saying {لاَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ} on this has several views. One: that it is a ḥāl from the first «مَنْ», or the second, or both together. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "A ḥāl, either from the first or the second, according to the one who makes it nominative by the adverbial phrase." He means that if we make «مَنْ» in His saying {وَلَهُ مَن فِي السماوات} nominative as agent, the nominating factor being the adverbial phrase, which is the view of al-Akhfash, then «لا يَسْتَكبرون» may be a ḥāl from either the first «مَنْ» or the second, because a ḥāl comes from the agent. The implication is that if we make it a mubtadaʾ, «يستكبرون» cannot be a ḥāl, as though he holds that a ḥāl does not come from a mubtadaʾ, which is the view of some. On the issue there is discussion established elsewhere. «لا يستكبرون» may be a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «عندَه», which is a ṣila, or a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «له», which is the khabar.
The second of the two views about «مَنْ»: that it is a mubtadaʾ and «لا يستكبرون» its khabar, this being a sentence conjoined to the preceding one. Is the sentence {وَلَهُ مَن فِي السماوات} resumptive, or does it balance the sentence {وَلَكُمُ الويل}, i.e. "to you is woe, and to Allah the Exalted belongs the whole world, upper and lower"? The first is clearer.
«ولا يَسْتَحْسِرون» means: they do not tire or grow weary. It is said «استحسر البعيرُ», i.e. the camel grew weary and tired. ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbada said: 3333 - «بها جِيَفُ الحسرى فأمَّا عِظامُها ... فبِيْضٌ وأمَّا جِلْدُها فصَلِيْبُ» (In it are carcasses of the exhausted: as for their bones, they are white; as for their hide, it is hard). It is also said «حَسَر البعيرُ» and «حَسَرْته أنا», so it is both intransitive and transitive; and «أَحْسَرْتُه» also, so «فَعَل» and «أَفْعَلَ» have one meaning in one of the two senses of «فَعَل». al-Zamakhsharī said: "«الاستحسار» is an intensification of «الحُسور» (weariness). So the most emphatic way of describing them was to negate from them the least weariness." I say: in «الاستحسار» there is a clarification that what they are engaged in would entail the utmost weariness, and that they are well suited, by those overwhelming acts of worship, to become weary in what they do. This is a fine question and a fitting answer.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {يُسَبِّحُونَ}: it may be resumptive, or a ḥāl from the agent in the preceding sentence. {لاَ يَفْتُرُونَ} may be resumptive, or a ḥāl from the agent of «يُسَبِّحون».

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {أَمِ اتخذوا}: this is the disconnected «أم» (munqaṭiʿa), implied as «بل», which marks a transition, together with the hamza meaning denial. «اتَّخذ» may mean «صَنَع» (made), so «مِن» is attached to it. The Shaykh allowed that it be the «صَيَّر» (made into) in His saying {واتخذ الله إِبْرَاهِيمَ خَلِيلاً} [al-Nisāʾ: 125]; he said: "In it is the meaning of choosing and selecting." {مِّنَ الأرض} may be attached to the taking, as before, or attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «آلهة», i.e. of the genus of the earth.
His saying: {هُمْ يُنشِرُونَ}: a sentence in the position of accusative as an adjective of «آلهة». The majority read «يُنْشِرون» with ḍamma on the imperfect prefix, from «أَنْشَر». al-Ḥasan read it with fatḥa and ḍamma on the shīn. It is said: «أَنْشَر اللهُ الموتى فَنَشَروا», and «نَشَر» is both intransitive and transitive.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ الله}: «إلاَّ» here is an adjective of the indefinite before it, with the meaning of «غَيْر». The iʿrāb in it is impossible, so it is put on what follows it. Describing by it has conditions, among them: the described is indefinite, or close to indefinite by being defined with the generic «ال»; and that it be an explicit plural as in the verse, or what is equivalent to a plural, as in the saying: 3334 - «لو كان غيري سُلَيْمى اليومَ غيَّره ... وَقْعُ الحوادِثِ إلاَّ الصارمُ الذَّكَرُ» (Had it been someone other than me, Sulaymā, that the blows of events changed today, except the sharp, male blade), where «إلاَّ الصارِمُ» is an adjective of «غيري» because it has the sense of a plural; and that its described not be omitted, the reverse of «غير». We have perfected all this in «Īḍāḥ al-sabīl ilā sharḥ al-Tasḥīl», so refer to it. Sībawayh recited on that the poet's saying: 3335 - «وكلُّ أخٍ مُفارِقُه أخُوه ... لَعَمْرُ أبيكَ إلاَّ الفرقدانِ» (Every brother is left by his brother, by your father's life, except the two Farqads [stars]), i.e. every brother other than the two Farqads is left by his brother. Description by «إلاَّ» has occurred as exception by «غير» has occurred, though the basis of «إلاَّ» is exception and of «غير» description. Among the elegant sayings of Abū l-Qāsim al-Zamakhsharī: "Know that «إلاَّ» and «غير» lend to one another."
It is not permissible that the Divine Name be nominative as a badal of «آلهة», because the meaning would be corrupted. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what prevented you from nominative as badal? I say: because «لو» is like «إنْ» in that the speech with it is affirmative, and the badal is permissible only in non-affirmative speech, as in the saying of the Exalted {وَلاَ يَلْتَفِتْ مِنكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ امرأتك} [Hūd: 81]; for the most general of the general can be negated but cannot be affirmed." So he made the obstacle technical, based on the invalidity of affirming the most general of the general.
Better than this is what Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned from the angle of meaning, saying: "It cannot be a badal, because the meaning would come to your saying: 'had Allah been in them, they would have been corrupted'. Do you not see that if you said «ما جاءني قومُك إلاَّ زيدٌ» as a badal, the meaning would be: 'Zayd alone came to me'?" Then he mentioned the point by which al-Zamakhsharī rejected it, saying: "It is said: the badal is barred because before it is an affirmation." Abū l-Baqāʾ barred the accusative of exception for two reasons. One: that it is corrupt in meaning; for when you say «لو جاءني القومُ إلاَّ زيداً لقتلتُهم», its meaning is that the killing was prevented by Zayd's being with the people. So if it were accusative in the verse, the meaning would be that the corruption of the heavens and the earth was prevented by the existence of Allah the Exalted with the gods, and in that is the affirmation of a god with Allah. When it is nominative as an adjective, nothing like that follows, because the meaning is: had there been in them other than Allah, they would have been corrupted. The second reason: that «آلهة» here is indefinite, and a plural, when indefinite, is not excepted from, according to a group of the verifiers, since it has no generality such that the excepted would be included in it were it not for the exception.
This view, which the two of them barred, I mean al-Zamakhsharī and Abū l-Baqāʾ, was allowed by Abū l-ʿAbbās al-Mubarrad and others. As for al-Mubarrad, he said: "The badal is allowed because what comes after «لو» is non-affirmative in meaning, and the badal in non-affirmative speech is better than the adjective." In this there is room for objection from the angle of what Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned about the corruption of meaning.
Ibn al-Ḍāʾiʿ, following al-Mubarrad, said: "The meaning is not valid to my mind unless «إلاَّ» has the meaning of «غير» by which substitution is meant, i.e. 'had there been in them gods in place of one, i.e. instead of the One who is Allah, they would have been corrupted'. This is the meaning Sībawayh intended in the issue he brought as a preface."
al-Shalawbīn said, on Sībawayh's issue «لو كان معنا رجلٌ إلاَّ زيدٌ لَغُلِبْنا» ('had there been with us a man other than Zayd we would have been defeated'): "The meaning is: had there been with us a man in place of Zayd we would have been defeated, so «إلاَّ» has the meaning of «غير» which means 'in place of'." This is also an inclination by Abū ʿAlī toward the badal. What Ibn al-Ḍāʾiʿ mentioned of the preceding meaning justifies the badal. It is an answer to what Abū l-Baqāʾ used to corrupt the badal view, since its meaning is clear, but it is close to an explanation of the meaning rather than an explanation of the iʿrāb.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {هذا ذِكْرُ مَن مَّعِيَ}: The majority read «ذِكْر» annexed to «مَنْ», the annexation of the maṣdar to its object, like the saying of the Exalted {بِسُؤَالِ نَعْجَتِكَ} [Ṣād: 24]. «ذِكْرٌ» has been read with tanwīn in both places, with «مَنْ» having fatḥa on the mīm: the maṣdar takes tanwīn and governs the object in the accusative, like the saying of the Exalted {أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً} [al-Balad: 14-15].
Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read «ذِكْرٌ» with tanwīn and «مِنْ» with kasra on the mīm. There are two interpretations of this. One: that there is an omitted described element whose adjective, the adverbial phrase, stands in its place; the implied form: "this is a mention from a book with me, and from a book before me". The second: that «معي» means «عندي»; the entry of «مِنْ» on «مع» is rare, because it is an adverb that is not declined. Abū Ḥātim declared this reading weak and saw no justification for «مِنْ» entering «مع».
Ṭalḥa read «ذِكْرٌ معي وذكرٌ قبلي» with tanwīn on both, without «مِنْ» in either. A group read «ذكرُ مَنْ» annexed to «مَنْ» like the majority, and «وذكرٌ مِنْ قبلُ» with tanwīn and kasra on the mīm of «مِنْ». Its explanation is clear from what preceded.
His saying: {لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ الحق}: The majority read «الحق» accusative. Two views: the clearer, that it is a direct object of the preceding verb; the second, that it is a confirmatory maṣdar. al-Zamakhsharī said: "The accusative may also be as emphasis of the content of the preceding sentence, as you say «هذا عبدُ الله الحقَّ لا الباطل», so he emphasized the negation of knowledge."
al-Ḥasan, Ibn Muḥayṣin and Ḥumayd read «الحق» nominative. Two views: one, that it is a mubtadaʾ with an implied khabar; the second, that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. al-Zamakhsharī said: "«الحقُّ» has been read nominative, with the emphasis placed between the cause and the caused. The meaning: their turning away because of ignorance is the truth, not falsehood."

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {بَلْ عِبَادٌ}: «عبادٌ» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are servants". «مُكْرَمون» is light in the majority reading, and the reading of ʿIkrima is with shadda.

semin-durr:27-27.t: His saying: {لاَ يَسْبِقُونَهُ}: a sentence in the position of nominative as an adjective of «عبادٌ». The majority read the bāʾ of «يَسْبِقونه» with kasra; it has also been read with ḍamma. This was explained as the imperfect of «سَبَقه», i.e. "he overcame him in racing". It is said «سابقه فَسَبقه يَسْبُقه», i.e. he overcame him in the race. The imperfect of «فَعَلَ» in contest has ḍamma on the ʿayn without exception, except for verbs with yāʾ as the ʿayn or the lām. What is meant: "they do not precede Him in speech"; the alif and lām compensate for the ḍamma according to the Kufans, and the pronoun is omitted according to the Basrans, i.e. "in the speech from Him".

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {فذلك نَجْزِيهِ}: two views are allowed for «ذلك». One: that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and this is a good view. The second: that it is accusative by an implied verb which this overt one explains; the issue belongs to the chapter of preoccupation (ishtighāl). In this view there is the implication of a governing verb while it is dispensable, so it is the less preferred. The fāʾ and what is within its scope are in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the condition. «كذلك» is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar or a ḥāl from the pronoun of the maṣdar, i.e. "a recompense like that recompense", or "We recompense with the recompense while it is like that".
The majority read «نجزي» with fatḥa on the nūn; Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ read it with ḍamma. Its explanation is that it is from «أجزأ» with hamza, from «أجزأني كذا», i.e. it sufficed me; then the hamza was lightened and turned into yāʾ.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {أَوَلَمْ يَرَ}: Ibn Kathīr read «ألم يرَ» without wāw. The rest read it with the wāw between the interrogative hamza and «لم». The like of the omission and retention of the wāw here has preceded in al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān, in the saying {قَالُواْ اتخذ الله وَلَداً} [al-Baqara: 116] and {سارعوا إلى مَغْفِرَةٍ} [al-Baqara: 133 (sic)], and its rule has been discussed. [Translator's note: the source cites the second example as al-Baqara; it occurs at Āl ʿImrān 133. Translated as written.] The "seeing" here may be of the heart or of the eye. «أنَّ» and what is within its scope fill the place of two objects according to the majority on the first, the place of one with the second omitted according to al-Akhfash, and the place of one only on the second.
His saying: {كَانَتَا}: the pronoun refers to the heavens and the earth in the dual form, though the antecedent is plural. There are several views on this. One: what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned, saying: "It was said «كانتا» and not «كُنَّ» because what is meant is the group of the heavens and the group of the earths. Of this is their saying «لِقاحان سَوْداوان», i.e. two groups. He did with the pronoun what he did with the overt noun." The second: Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The pronoun refers to the two genera." The third: al-Ḥūfī said: "He said «كانتا رَتْقاً», and «السماوات» is a plural, because he meant the two kinds. al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur said: 3336 - «إن المنيَّةَ والحُتُوفَ كِلاهما ... يُوفي المخارم يَرْقُبان سوادي» (Death and deadly fates, both of them, stand on the mountain passes watching for me), because he meant the two kinds." Ibn ʿAṭiyya followed him in this, saying: "He said «وكانتا» in that they are two kinds." Like it is the saying of ʿAmr ibn Shuyaym: 3337 - «ألم يُحْزِنْكَ أنَّ حبالَ قيسٍ ... وتَغْلِبَ قد تباينتا انقطاعا» (Does it not grieve you that the ropes of Qays and Taghlib have separated, broken apart?).
«رَتْقاً» is the khabar. It is not made dual because it is originally a maṣdar. Then you may make it stand in place of the object, like «الخَلْق» meaning «المَخْلوق», or make it with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "two having sealedness". This is the reading of the majority.
al-Ḥasan, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Abū Ḥaywa and ʿĪsā read «رَتَقاً» with fatḥa on the tāʾ. Two views: one, that it is also a maṣdar, so it has the two views mentioned for the one with sukūn on the tāʾ. The second: that it is «فَعَل» with the meaning of «مَفْعول», like «القَبَض» and «النَّقَض» meaning "the seized" and "the broken"; on this its khabar should have agreed in the dual. al-Zamakhsharī answered that, saying: "It is on the implication of a described noun, i.e. 'they were a sealed thing'." Some preferred the maṣdar view on account of the lack of agreement in the dual, and you have learned its answer. He may say: the basis is the non-omission of the described, so one does not resort to it without necessity.
«الرَّتْق» is joining together. «ارْتَتَقَ حَلْقُه» means it closed up. A woman is «رَتْقاء», i.e. one whose vulva is closed, so intercourse with her was not possible because of that. «الفَتْق» is the separation of that joined thing, and it is one of the finest figures of badīʿ here, in that He set «الرَّتْق» against «الفَتْق». al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: when did they see the two sealed, such that their being asked to affirm it came? I say: there are two views. One: that it occurs in the Qurʾān, which is a miracle in itself, so it stands in the place of the seen, the witnessed. The second: that the heaven and earth clinging together and their being apart are both rationally possible, so the being apart rather than clinging needs a specifier, who is the Eternal, glory be to Him."
His saying: {وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ المآء كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ}: this «جَعَل» may mean «خلق», taking one object, which is «كلَّ شيءٍ», and {مِنَ المآء} is attached to the preceding verb. It may be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «كل شيء», because originally it could be its description, but when put before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl. The meaning of His creating it from water is one of two things: either the intense need of every animal for water, so it cannot live without it; or that it is created from the sperm-drop (nuṭfa), which is called water. «جَعَل» may mean «صَيَّر», taking two objects, the second the prepositional phrase, in the sense that We made every living thing depend on water, which it cannot do without.
The majority read «حيّ» genitive as an adjective of «شَيْء». Ḥumayd read it accusative as the second object of «جَعَلْنا», with the adverbial phrase idle (laghw). On this reading it is remote that «جعل» mean «خَلَقَ», or that «حَيَّاً» be accusative as ḥāl.
